sentences.zh: 推入紀法：置上元庚辰盡所求年，以元法除之，不滿元法，以紀法除之，余不滿紀法，入紀年也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing entry into an era: set the years from the superior origin gengchen through the year sought; divide by the origin divisor; what does not fill the origin divisor, divide by the era divisor; the remainder that does not fill the era divisor is the years entered within the era.
translations.idiomatic: To find which era a year falls in, count from the gengchen superior origin through the target year, divide by 3,648, then divide the remainder by 608; the final remainder is the year within that era.

sentences.zh: 滿法去之，得後紀。

translations.literal: When it fills the divisor, remove it and obtain the next era.
translations.idiomatic: When a divisor is fully exhausted, drop it and advance to the following era.

sentences.zh: 入甲午紀壬辰歲來，至今元嘉二十年歲在癸末，二百三十一年，算外。

translations.literal: From entering the Jiawu Era in the year renchen to the present, Yuanjia year 20 in the year guiwei, is 231 years, outside the reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: From entry into the Jiawu Era (renchen year) down to the present Yuanjia year 20 (guiwei) is 231 years, exclusive in the count.

sentences.zh: 推積月術：置入紀年數算外，以章月乘之，如章歲為積月，不盡為閏餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing accumulated months: set the years entered within the era, outside the reckoning; multiply by rule months and divide by rule years for accumulated months; what does not exhaust is the intercalary remainder.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated months, take the years within the current era (exclusive count), multiply by 235, divide by 19; the quotient is total months, the remainder the leap fraction.

sentences.zh: 閏餘十二以上，其年閏。

translations.literal: If the intercalary remainder is twelve or more, that year is intercalary.
translations.idiomatic: A leap year occurs when the intercalary remainder reaches twelve or higher.

sentences.zh: 推朔術：以通數乘積分，為朔積分，滿日法為積日，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing new moons: multiply accumulated months by the communication number for the accumulated new-moon fraction; when it fills the day divisor it becomes accumulated days; what does not exhaust is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To compute conjunction instants, multiply accumulated months by 22,207; divide by 752 for whole days; the residue is the fractional day.

sentences.zh: 以六旬去積日，不盡為大餘，命以紀，算外，所求年正月朔日也。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated days; what does not exhaust is the large remainder; count by the era, outside the reckoning: this is the new-moon day of the first month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the day count modulo sixty for the sexagenary index, then name the day against the era cycle: that is the first-month conjunction of the target year.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加大餘二十九，小餘三百九十九，小余滿日法從大餘，即次月朔也。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add to the large remainder twenty-nine and to the small remainder three hundred ninety-nine; when the small remainder fills the day divisor, carry to the large remainder: this is the next month's conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add 29 to the day count and 399 to the fraction, carrying overflows by 752 into the day count.

sentences.zh: 小餘三百五十三以上，其月大也。

translations.literal: If the small remainder is three hundred fifty-three or more, that month is long.
translations.idiomatic: If the fractional part is 353 or greater, the month is a long thirty-day month.

sentences.zh: 推弦望法：加朔大餘七，小餘二百八十七，小分三，小分滿四從小余，小余滿日法從大餘，命如前，上弦日也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing quarter- and full-moons: add to the new-moon large remainder seven, to the small remainder two hundred eighty-seven, and three small parts; when small parts fill four, carry to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the day divisor, carry to the large remainder; count as before: this is the first-quarter day.
translations.idiomatic: For the first quarter add 7 days, 287 parts, and 3 small parts to the new-moon remainder, carrying at 4 small parts and at 752 parts per day, then read off the date as before.

sentences.zh: 又加之得望，又加之得下弦。

translations.literal: Add again to obtain full moon, and add again to obtain last quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the same addition to reach full moon, and once more for last quarter.

sentences.zh: 推二十四氣術：置入紀年算外，以餘數乘之，滿度法三百四為積沒，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the twenty-four qi: set the years entered within the era, outside the reckoning; multiply by the remainder number; when it fills the degree divisor 304 it becomes accumulated extinction; what does not exhaust is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: For the twenty-four solar terms, take years within the era (exclusive), multiply by 1,595, divide by 304 for whole cycles; the remainder is the fractional part.

sentences.zh: 以六旬去積沒，不盡為大餘，命以紀，算外，所求年雨水日也。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated extinction; what does not exhaust is the large remainder; count by the era, outside the reckoning: this is the Rain Water day of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce modulo sixty for the stem-branch index and name against the era: that gives Rain Water for the target year.

sentences.zh: 求次氣，加大餘十五，小餘六十六，小分十一，小分滿氣法從小余，小余滿度法從大餘，次氣日也。

translations.literal: To seek the next qi, add to the large remainder fifteen, to the small remainder sixty-six, and eleven small parts; when small parts fill the qi divisor, carry to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the degree divisor, carry to the large remainder: this is the next qi day.
translations.idiomatic: For the following term add 15 days, 66 parts, and 11 small parts, carrying at 24 small parts and at 304 parts per day.

sentences.zh: 雨水在十六日以後者，如法減之，得立春。

translations.literal: If Rain Water falls after the sixteenth day, reduce according to the method to obtain Beginning of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: When Rain Water would fall after the sixteenth, apply the prescribed reduction to obtain Beginning of Spring instead.

sentences.zh: 推閏月法：以閏余減章歲，餘以歲中乘之，滿章閏得一，數從正月起，閏所在也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing intercalary months: subtract the intercalary remainder from rule years; multiply the remainder by mid-year qi; when it fills rule intercalations obtain one; count from the first month: there lies the intercalation.
translations.idiomatic: For the leap month, subtract the leap fraction from 19, multiply the result by 12, divide by 7; count forward from the first month by the quotient to locate the intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 閏有進退，以無中氣禦之。

translations.literal: Intercalation may advance or retreat; regulate it by the absence of a mid-climate.
translations.idiomatic: Leap placement may need adjustment; the month without a major solar term governs the decision.

sentences.zh: 推沒滅術：因雨水積，以沒餘乘之，滿沒法為大餘，不盡為小餘，如前，所求年為雨水前沒日也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing extinction and disappearance: take the Rain Water accumulation; multiply by the extinction remainder; when it fills the extinction divisor it becomes the large remainder; what does not exhaust is the small remainder; as before: this is the extinction day before Rain Water of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: For extinction days before Rain Water, multiply the Rain Water accumulation by 36 and divide by 319 for the day index and remainder, naming the date as before.

sentences.zh: 求次沒，加大餘六十九，小餘一百九十六，滿沒法從大餘，命如前，雨水後沒日也。

translations.literal: To seek the next extinction, add to the large remainder sixty-nine and to the small remainder one hundred ninety-six; when it fills the extinction divisor, carry to the large remainder; count as before: this is the extinction day after Rain Water.
translations.idiomatic: For the next extinction add 69 days and 196 parts, carrying at 319 parts per day, then read off the post-Rain Water extinction.

sentences.zh: 雨水前沒多在故歲，常有五沒，官以沒正之，一年常有五沒或六沒。

translations.literal: Extinctions before Rain Water mostly fall in the previous year; there are regularly five extinctions; the office corrects by extinction; in one year there are regularly five or six extinctions.
translations.idiomatic: Pre-Rain Water extinctions usually belong to the prior civil year; five such days are normal, and the bureau aligns the calendar accordingly—five or six per year is standard.

sentences.zh: 小餘盡為滅日也。

translations.literal: When the small remainder is exhausted, it is a disappearance day.
translations.idiomatic: When the fractional part reaches zero, that day is a disappearance (mie) day.

sentences.zh: 雨水小餘三十九以還，雨水六旬後乃有。

translations.literal: If Rain Water's small remainder is thirty-nine or less, only after six decades following Rain Water does one appear.
translations.idiomatic: When Rain Water's fraction is 39 or below, the next such event does not occur until sixty days after Rain Water.

sentences.zh: 推土用事法：置立春大小餘小分之數，減大餘十八，小餘七十九，小分十八，命以紀，算外，立春前土用事日也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the reign of Earth: set the Beginning of Spring large and small remainders and small parts; subtract from the large remainder eighteen, from the small remainder seventy-nine, and from the small parts eighteen; count by the era, outside the reckoning: this is the day Earth takes reign before Beginning of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: For Earth taking reign before Beginning of Spring, take the spring-term remainders, subtract 18 days, 79 parts, and 18 small parts, and name the date against the era cycle.

sentences.zh: 大餘不足加六十，小餘不足減，減大餘一，加度法而後減之。

translations.literal: If the large remainder is insufficient, add sixty; if the small remainder is insufficient to subtract, subtract one from the large remainder, add the degree divisor, and then subtract.
translations.idiomatic: Borrow 60 days when the day count runs short; borrow one degree-divisor (304 parts) per day when fractions underflow.

sentences.zh: 立夏、立冬求土用事皆如上法。

translations.literal: Beginning of Summer and Beginning of Winter: seek Earth's reign by the same method as above.
translations.idiomatic: For Beginning of Summer and Beginning of Winter, compute Earth's reign by the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 推日所在度法：以度法乘朔積度，不盡為分。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the du where the sun stands: multiply the accumulated new-moon du by the degree divisor; what does not exhaust is the parts.
translations.idiomatic: To find the sun's ecliptic longitude at conjunction, multiply the accumulated conjunction degrees by 304; the remainder is fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 命度起室二，次宿除之，算外，正月朔夜半日在度及分也。

translations.literal: Count the du starting from Room II; remove successive lodges; outside the reckoning: at midnight on the first-month new moon, the sun's du and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Index from Room 2 through the lodges; the result is the sun's position at midnight on the first-month new moon.

sentences.zh: 求次日，日加一度，經室去度分。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, add one du per day; when passing Room, remove the degree parts.
translations.idiomatic: For each following day add one du; when crossing the Room lodge, apply the prescribed part reduction.

sentences.zh: 推月所在度法：以月周乘朔積日，周天去之，余滿度法為積度，不盡為分，命度如前，正月朔夜半月所在度及分。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the du where the moon stands: multiply accumulated new-moon days by the lunar circuit; remove the circumference of Heaven; the remainder, when it fills the degree divisor, is accumulated du; what does not exhaust is parts; count the du as before: at midnight on the first-month new moon, the moon's du and parts.
translations.idiomatic: For the moon's position, multiply conjunction days by 4,064, reduce modulo 111,025, divide by 304 for du and parts, and index from Room 2 as before.

sentences.zh: 求次月，小月加度二十二，分一百三十三，大月加度三十五，分二百四十五，分滿度法成一度，命如前，次月朔月所在度及分也。

translations.literal: To seek the next month: for a short month add du twenty-two and parts one hundred thirty-three; for a long month add du thirty-five and parts two hundred forty-five; when parts fill the degree divisor, form one du; count as before: the next month's new-moon du and parts.
translations.idiomatic: For the next month add 22 du 133 parts (short month) or 35 du 245 parts (long month), carrying at 304 parts per du.

sentences.zh: 曆先月法：以十六除月行分為大分，如所入遲疾加之，經室去度分。

translations.literal: Calendar preceding-month method: divide the moon's motion parts by sixteen for large parts; add according to the slow-fast entered; when passing Room, remove the degree parts.
translations.idiomatic: In the month-ahead procedure, divide lunar motion parts by 16, add the entered anomaly correction, and reduce when crossing Room.

sentences.zh: 推合朔月食術：置所求年積月，以會數一百六十乘之，以所入交會紀差二十二加之，滿會月去之，餘則其年正月朔去交分也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing conjunction new moons and lunar eclipses: set the accumulated months of the year sought; multiply by the coincidence number 160; add the crossing-coincidence era-difference of the era entered, 22; when it fills coincidence months, remove it; the remainder is the first-month new moon's distance from crossing in parts.
translations.idiomatic: For syzygy and eclipse limits, multiply year lunations by 160, add the nodal offset for the current era (22 for this cycle), and reduce modulo 929 for the first month's nodal distance.

sentences.zh: 求次月，以會數加之，滿會月去之。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add the coincidence number; when it fills coincidence months, remove it.
translations.idiomatic: For each following month add 160 and reduce modulo 929.

sentences.zh: 求望，加合數。

translations.literal: To seek full moon, add the conjunction number.
translations.idiomatic: For full moon add the conjunction number (80).

sentences.zh: 朔望去交分如合數以下，交限數以上，朔則交會，望則月食。

translations.literal: If the new- or full-moon distance from crossing is at or below the conjunction number but at or above the crossing-limit number, at new moon there is crossing-coincidence; at full moon, lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: When nodal distance is between 80 and 859, new moon yields a solar eclipse and full moon a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 推入遲疾曆法：置所求年朔積分，所入遲疾差一萬五千二百四十五加之，滿通周去之，余滿日法得一日，不盡為日餘，命日算外，所求年正月朔入曆。

translations.literal: Method for pushing entry into the slow-fast calendar: set the accumulated new-moon fraction of the year sought; add the slow-fast difference of the era entered, 15,245; when it fills the communication circuit, remove it; the remainder, when it fills the day divisor, gives one day; what does not exhaust is the day-remainder; count the day, outside the reckoning: entry into the calendar for the first-month new moon of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: For lunar anomaly entry at the year's first conjunction, add the era's anomaly offset (15,245 for Jiawu), reduce modulo 20,721, then divide by 752 for days and remainder.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加一日，日餘七百三十四。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add one day and day-remainder seven hundred thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add 1 day and 734 parts.

sentences.zh: 求望，加十四日，日餘五百七十五半。

translations.literal: To seek full moon, add fourteen days and day-remainder five hundred seventy-five and a half.
translations.idiomatic: For full moon add 14 days and 575½ parts.

sentences.zh: 余滿日法成一日，日滿二十七去之，除日余如周日日餘，不足減，減一日，加周虛。

translations.literal: When the remainder fills the day divisor, form one day; when days fill twenty-seven, remove them; for the day-remainder, if it is like the circuit-day day-remainder and insufficient to subtract, subtract one day and add the circuit void.
translations.idiomatic: Carry at 752 parts per day; reduce days modulo 27; at circuit day apply the 417-part remainder rule, borrowing a day and adding 335 when needed.

sentences.zh: 日滿二十七而日余不滿周日日餘，為損。

translations.literal: When days fill twenty-seven but the day-remainder does not fill the circuit-day day-remainder, it is a decrease.
translations.idiomatic: When the day count reaches 27 but the remainder has not reached 417, apply the decrease rule.

sentences.zh: 周日滿去之，為入曆一日。

translations.literal: When the circuit day is full, remove it; this is entry into the calendar for one day.
translations.idiomatic: When the circuit-day condition is satisfied, drop it and count one day of calendar entry.

sentences.zh: 推合朔月食定大小餘法：以入曆日餘乘入曆下損益率，入一日，益二十五是也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the fixed large and small remainders for conjunction and lunar eclipse: multiply the day-remainder entered in the calendar by the decrease-increase rate below the calendar entry; entering day one, an increase of twenty-five is correct.
translations.idiomatic: To fix new- and full-moon remainders for syzygy and eclipse, multiply the entered day-fraction by the anomaly table's excess-deficit rate; on day 1 the rate is +25.

sentences.zh: 以損益盈縮積分，值損則損之，值益則益之。

translations.literal: Use it to decrease-increase the surplus-shrinkage accumulated fraction; where it hits decrease, decrease; where it hits increase, increase.
translations.idiomatic: Apply that rate to the surplus-shrinkage accumulator, subtracting on deficit rows and adding on excess rows.

sentences.zh: 為定積分。

translations.literal: This becomes the fixed accumulated fraction.
translations.idiomatic: The result is the corrected accumulated fraction.

sentences.zh: 以入曆日餘乘列差，滿日法盈減縮加差法，為定差法。

translations.literal: Multiply the day-remainder entered in the calendar by the column difference; when it fills the day divisor, for surplus subtract from the difference method and for shrinkage add to the difference method: this is the fixed difference method.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the entered day-fraction by the column difference, divide by 752, and adjust the difference divisor by the surplus or shrinkage sign.

sentences.zh: 以除定積分，所得減加本朔望小餘，值盈則減，縮則加之。

translations.literal: Divide the fixed accumulated fraction by it; what is obtained, subtract from or add to the original new- and full-moon small remainder; where surplus, subtract; where shrinkage, add.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the corrected accumulator by that divisor and apply the quotient to the base conjunction fraction, subtracting for surplus and adding for shrinkage.

sentences.zh: 為定小餘。

translations.literal: This is the fixed small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: That yields the corrected fractional day.

sentences.zh: 加之滿日法，合朔月食進一日；

translations.literal: If adding fills the day divisor, conjunction and lunar eclipse advance one day.
translations.idiomatic: If the correction carries past 752 parts, advance the syzygy one day.

sentences.zh: 減之不足減者，加日法而後減之，則退一日。

translations.literal: If subtracting is insufficient to subtract, add the day divisor and then subtract: then retreat one day.
translations.idiomatic: If subtraction underflows, borrow 752 parts and push the date back one day.

sentences.zh: 值周日者，用周日定數。

translations.literal: When it hits a circuit day, use the circuit-day fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: On a circuit day use the special circuit-day correction.

sentences.zh: 推加時：以十二乘定小余，滿日法得一辰，數從子起，算外，則朔望加時所在辰也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the double-hour: multiply the fixed small remainder by twelve; when it fills the day divisor obtain one chen; count from zi outward, outside the reckoning: this is the chen where the new- or full-moon hour falls.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the corrected fraction by twelve and divide by 752 to name the twelve double-hours from midnight.

sentences.zh: 有餘者四之，滿日法得一為少，二為半，三為太半。

translations.literal: If there is remainder, quadruple it; when it fills the day divisor obtain one shao, two makes ban, three makes tai.
translations.idiomatic: Split the leftover into quarters of the divisor for the shao, ban, and tai subdivisions.

sentences.zh: 又有餘者三之，滿日法得一為強，半法以上排成一，不滿半法棄之。

translations.literal: If again there is remainder, triple it; when it fills the day divisor obtain one qiang; if it fills half the divisor or more, advance one notch; if it does not fill half the divisor, discard it.
translations.idiomatic: Further triple the tail to reach the strong step, rounding up at half-divisor.

sentences.zh: 以強並少為少強，並半為半強，並太為太強。

translations.literal: Combine qiang with shao to make shao-qiang; combine with ban to make ban-qiang; combine with tai to make tai-qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Add strong units to weak, half, or full subdivisions per the classical clepsydra notation.

sentences.zh: 得二者為小弱，以並少為半弱，以並半為太弱，以並太為一辰弱。

translations.literal: Obtaining two qiang makes shao-ruo; with it combine shao to make ban-ruo; with it combine ban to make tai-ruo; with it combine tai to make one chen-ruo.
translations.idiomatic: Two strongs collapse into a weak grade, stepping through the ladder to a full weak double-hour mark.

sentences.zh: 以所在辰名之。

translations.literal: Name it by the chen where it stands.
translations.idiomatic: Read the final label against the stem hour.

sentences.zh: 推合朔月食加時滿刻法：各以百刻乘定小餘，如日法而一；

translations.literal: Method for pushing the full clepsydra marks for conjunction and lunar eclipse hours: for each, multiply the fixed small remainder by one hundred clepsydra marks and divide by the day divisor.
translations.idiomatic: For syzygy and eclipse times, scale the corrected fraction to 100 day-parts by dividing by 752.

sentences.zh: 不盡什之，求分。

translations.literal: What does not exhaust, decimate it to seek the parts.
translations.idiomatic: Express the remainder in tenths for the fractional mark.

sentences.zh: 先除夜漏之半，即晝漏加時刻及分也。

translations.literal: First remove half the night clepsydra: this is the day clepsydra hour and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract half the night-water total to obtain the daytime hour and parts.

sentences.zh: 晝漏盡，又入夜漏。

translations.literal: When the day clepsydra is exhausted, one again enters the night clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: After the day portion is used up, count into the night clepsydra.

sentences.zh: 在中節前後四日以還者，視限數。

translations.literal: If within four days on either side of a mid-term node, consult the limit number.
translations.idiomatic: When a syzygy falls within four days of a major solar term, consult the tight limit number.

sentences.zh: 在中節前後五日以上者，視間限數。

translations.literal: If five or more days before or after a mid-term node, consult the gap-limit number.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond five days from the major term, apply the wider gap-limit rule.

sentences.zh: 月食加時定小餘不滿限數、間數者，皆以算上為日。

translations.literal: If the fixed small remainder for the lunar-eclipse hour does not fill the limit number or gap-limit number, all count upward as a day.
translations.idiomatic: When the eclipse fraction falls under both margin thresholds, promote the count to the next day.

translations.idiomatic: For syzygy longitude, multiply the conjunction fraction by 19 and divide by 47 for large and small parts.

sentences.zh: 以大分從朔夜半日日分，滿度命如前，正月朔日月合朔所在共合度也。

translations.literal: Let the large parts follow the new-moon midnight day-parts; when they fill the du, count as before: at the first-month new moon, the sun and moon share the conjunction du.
translations.idiomatic: Add those parts to the midnight sun position and index through the lodges to obtain the shared solar-lunar longitude at the first-month conjunction.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加度二十九，大分一百六十一，小分十四，小分滿通法從大分，大分滿度法從度。

translations.idiomatic: When crossing the Room lodge, apply the prescribed part reduction.

translations.literal: To seek full moon, add fourteen du, large parts two hundred thirty-two, small parts thirty and a half.
translations.idiomatic: For full moon add 14° plus 232 large and 30½ small parts.

sentences.zh: 求望月所在度，加日度一百八十二，分一百八十九，小分二十三半。

translations.literal: Earth's later origin: jiaxu; Yuanjia year 11 to Yuanjia year 20 guiwei is ten years in the count.
translations.idiomatic: Earth's sub-epoch begins jiaxu; from Yuanjia 11 to Yuanjia 20 is ten years on the count.

sentences.zh: 金後元甲申，晉太元九年，至元嘉二十年癸未，六十年算上。

translations.literal: Metal's later origin: jiashen; Jin Taiyuan year 9 to Yuanjia year 20 guiwei is sixty years in the count.
translations.idiomatic: Metal's sub-epoch begins jiashen; from Jin Taiyuan 9 to Yuanjia 20 is sixty years on the count.

sentences.zh: 水後元乙丑，元嘉二年，至元嘉二十年癸未，十九年算上。

translations.literal: Water's later origin: yichou; Yuanjia year 2 to Yuanjia year 20 guiwei is nineteen years in the count.
translations.idiomatic: Water's sub-epoch begins yichou; from Yuanjia 2 to Yuanjia 20 is nineteen years on the count.

sentences.zh: 推五星法：各設其元至所求年算上，以合數乘之，滿合歲為積合，不盡曰合餘，多者以合數除之，得一，星合往年，得二，合前往年，不滿合數，其年。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the five planets: for each, set from its era-head to the year sought in the count; multiply by the conjunction number; when it fills conjunction years it becomes accumulated conjunction; what does not exhaust is called conjunction remainder; if large, divide by the conjunction number; obtaining one means the star conjoined the previous year, obtaining two means the year before that; if it does not fill the conjunction number, it is this year.
translations.idiomatic: For each planet, count from its sub-epoch to the target year, multiply by its conjunction number, and divide by its cycle length; the quotient gives prior conjunctions, the remainder locates the current conjunction year.

sentences.zh: 木、土、金則有往年合，火有前往年合，水一年三合或四合也。

translations.literal: Wood, Earth, and Metal can have a conjunction in the previous year; Fire can have one in the year before that; Water has three or four conjunctions in one year.
translations.idiomatic: Wood, Earth, and Metal may conjoin in the prior year; Fire may do so two years back; Water yields three or four conjunctions per year.

sentences.zh: 以合餘減合數為度分，水度分滿合歲則去之也。

translations.literal: Subtract the conjunction remainder from the conjunction number for degree parts; for Water, when degree parts fill conjunction years, remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the conjunction remainder from the conjunction number for ecliptic parts; for Water, reduce when parts exceed the synodic year.

sentences.zh: 以周天十一萬一千三十五乘度分，滿日度法為積度，不盡曰度餘。

translations.literal: Multiply degree parts by the circumference of Heaven 111,035; when it fills the day-degree divisor it becomes accumulated du; what does not exhaust is called du remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply those parts by 111,035 and divide by the day-degree divisor for accumulated degrees; the remainder is degree residue.

sentences.zh: 命度以室二，算外，星合所在度也。

translations.literal: Count the du starting from Room II, outside the reckoning: this is the du where the star conjoins.
translations.idiomatic: Index from Room 2 outward to name the conjunction longitude.

sentences.zh: 以合數乘其年，內雨水小餘，並度余為日余，滿日度法從積度為日，命以雨水，算外，星合日也。

translations.literal: Multiply the conjunction number by the years, add within the Rain Water small remainder, and combine with the du remainder for the day remainder; when it fills the day-degree divisor, carry to accumulated du for days; count from Rain Water, outside the reckoning: this is the star-conjunction day.
translations.idiomatic: Combine the synodic count with the Rain Water fraction and degree residue, carry into days, and name the date from Rain Water outward.

sentences.zh: 求星見日法，以法伏日及餘木則十六日及金是也。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the star's appearance day: use the hidden days and remainder—Wood uses sixteen days, and Metal is the same.
translations.idiomatic: For first visibility add the hiding interval—16 days for Wood and the same for Metal.

sentences.zh: 加星合日及余，滿日度法成一日，命如前，星見日也。

translations.literal: Add to the star-conjunction day and remainder; when it fills the day-degree divisor, form one day; count as before: this is the star-appearance day.
translations.idiomatic: Add that interval to the conjunction date, carry at the day-degree divisor, and read off the appearance day.

sentences.zh: 求星見度法，以法伏度及餘木則二度及餘是也。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the star's appearance du: use the hidden du and remainder—Wood uses two du and remainder.
translations.idiomatic: For appearance longitude add the hiding arc—2° plus residue for Wood.

sentences.zh: 加星合度及余，滿日度法成一度，命如前，所見度也。

translations.literal: Add to the star-conjunction du and remainder; when it fills the day-degree divisor, form one du; count as before: the du where it appears.
translations.idiomatic: Add to the conjunction longitude and carry at the day-degree divisor to obtain the visibility degree.

sentences.zh: 以星行分母木則二十三見也。

translations.literal: Use the star's motion denominator—Wood uses twenty-three appearances.
translations.idiomatic: Wood's motion divisor is based on 23 apparitions per cycle.

sentences.zh: 乘見度余，滿日度法得一，分乃日加所行分。

translations.literal: Multiply the appearance du remainder; when it fills the day-degree divisor obtain one; then add the motion parts day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Scale the appearance-degree remainder by the day-degree divisor and add daily motion parts thereafter.

sentences.zh: 木順日行四分。

translations.literal: Wood, direct motion: daily four parts.
translations.idiomatic: Wood in direct motion advances 4 parts per day.

sentences.zh: 分滿其母成一度，逆順母不同，木逆分母七也。

translations.literal: When parts fill their denominator they form one du; retrograde and direct denominators differ—Wood's retrograde denominator is seven.
translations.idiomatic: Parts carry into whole degrees at different denominators; Wood's retrograde divisor is 7.

sentences.zh: 當各乘度餘，留者承前，逆則減之，伏不書度，經室去分，不足減者，破全度。

translations.literal: Each should multiply the du remainder; if stationary, continue from before; if retrograde, subtract; during hiding do not record du; when passing Room remove parts; if insufficient to subtract, break a whole du.
translations.idiomatic: Apply the appropriate divisor to degree remainders; hold during stations, subtract in retrograde, omit degrees while hidden, reduce at Room, and borrow a full degree when needed.

sentences.zh: 五星室分各異，若在行分，各依室分去之。

translations.literal: The five planets' Room parts each differ; if in motion parts, each removes according to its Room part.
translations.idiomatic: Each planet has its own Room-lodge reduction when computing motion parts.

sentences.zh: 木：初與日合，伏，十六日，日余四萬一千七百八十，行二度，余七萬七千八百四十七半，晨見東方。

translations.literal: Wood: at first conjunction with the sun, it hides sixteen days, day-remainder 41,780, moving two du, remainder 77,847½; at dawn it appears in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Wood: at conjunction it hides 16 days with remainder 41,780, advancing 2° with residue 77,847½, then appears in the east at dawn.

sentences.zh: 去日十三度半強。

translations.literal: It stands thirteen and a half du strong from the sun.
translations.idiomatic: It stands 13½° strong east of the sun.

sentences.zh: 順，日行二十三分之四，一百一十五日行二十度。

translations.literal: Direct motion: daily twenty-three parts out of four; in 115 days it moves twenty du.
translations.idiomatic: Direct: 4/23 of a degree per day, 20° in 115 days.

sentences.zh: 留，不行，二十六日而逆。

translations.literal: Stationary, not moving, twenty-six days, then retrograde.
translations.idiomatic: It stations for 26 days, then turns retrograde.

sentences.zh: 日行七分之一，八十四日退十二度。

translations.literal: Daily one part out of seven; in 84 days it retreats twelve du.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde at 1/7° per day, retreating 12° in 84 days.

sentences.zh: 又留二十六日。

translations.literal: Again stationary twenty-six days.
translations.idiomatic: It stations again for 26 days.

sentences.zh: 順，一百一十五日行二十度，夕伏西方，日度余如初，與日合。

translations.literal: Direct motion: in 115 days it moves twenty du; at dusk it hides in the west; day and du remainder as at first, and conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Direct motion 20° in 115 days, then hides in the west at dusk with the same remainders as at first conjunction.

sentences.zh: 一終三百九十八日，日余八萬三千五百六十，行星三十三度，余五萬九千九百三十五。

translations.literal: One cycle: 398 days, day-remainder 83,560, planetary motion 33 du, remainder 59,935.
translations.idiomatic: One synodic cycle: 398 days with remainder 83,560, planetary travel 33° with residue 59,935.

sentences.zh: 火：初與日合，伏，七十一日，日余二萬四千八百一十二半，行五十四度，度余四萬九千四百三十，晨見東方。

translations.literal: Fire: at first conjunction with the sun, it hides seventy-one days, day-remainder 24,812½, moving fifty-four du, du-remainder 49,430; at dawn it appears in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Fire: hides 71 days with remainder 24,812½, advancing 54° with residue 49,430, then appears in the east at dawn.

sentences.zh: 去日十七度半強。

translations.literal: It stands seventeen and a half du strong from the sun.
translations.idiomatic: It stands 17½° strong east of the sun.

sentences.zh: 順，疾，日行七分之五，一百八日半行七十七度半。

translations.literal: Direct, fast: daily five parts out of seven; in 108½ days it moves 77½ du.
translations.idiomatic: Direct fast: 5/7° per day, 77½° in 108½ days.

sentences.zh: 小遲，日行七分之四，一百二十六日行七十二度而大遲。

translations.literal: Slightly slow: daily four parts out of seven; in 126 days it moves seventy-two du, then greatly slow.
translations.idiomatic: Slightly slow: 4/7° per day, 72° in 126 days, then very slow.

sentences.zh: 日行七分之二，四十二日行十二度。

translations.literal: Daily two parts out of seven; in 42 days it moves twelve du.
translations.idiomatic: Very slow: 2/7° per day, 12° in 42 days.

sentences.zh: 留，不行，十二日而遲。

translations.literal: Stationary, not moving, twelve days, then retrograde.
translations.idiomatic: It stations for 12 days, then turns retrograde.

sentences.zh: 日行十分之三，六十日退十八度。

translations.literal: Daily three parts out of ten; in 60 days it retreats eighteen du.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde at 3/10° per day, retreating 18° in 60 days.

sentences.zh: 又留十二日。

translations.literal: Again stationary twelve days.
translations.idiomatic: It stations again for 12 days.

sentences.zh: 順，遲，四十二日行十二度。

translations.literal: Direct, slow: in 42 days it moves twelve du.
translations.idiomatic: Direct slow: 12° in 42 days.

sentences.zh: 小疾，一百二十六日，行七十二度。

translations.literal: Slightly fast: in 126 days it moves seventy-two du.
translations.idiomatic: Slightly fast: 72° in 126 days.

sentences.zh: 一百八日半行七十七度半，夕伏西方，日度余如初，與日合。

translations.literal: In 108½ days it moves 77½ du; at dusk it hides in the west; day and du remainder as at first, and conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Fast direct motion 77½° in 108½ days, then hides in the west at dusk and reconjoins the sun.

sentences.zh: 一終七百七十九日，日余四萬九千六百二十五，行星四百一十四，度余三萬三千五百。

translations.literal: One cycle: 779 days, day-remainder 49,625, planetary motion 414, du-remainder 33,500.
translations.idiomatic: One synodic cycle: 779 days with remainder 49,625, planetary travel 414° with residue 33,500.

sentences.zh: 除一周，定四十九度，度余一萬七千三百七十五。

translations.literal: Remove one circuit; fixed 49 du, du-remainder 17,375.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce by one full circuit to 49° with residue 17,375.

sentences.zh: 土：初與日合，伏，十八日，日餘四千四百八十二半，行二度，度余四萬六千八百四十七半，晨見東方。

translations.literal: Earth: at first conjunction with the sun, it hides eighteen days, day-remainder 4,482½, moving two du, du-remainder 46,847½; at dawn it appears in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Earth: hides 18 days with remainder 4,482½, advancing 2° with residue 46,847½, then appears in the east at dawn.

sentences.zh: 去日十五度半強，順，日行十二分之一，八十四日，行七度。

translations.literal: It stands fifteen and a half du strong from the sun; direct, daily one part out of twelve; in 84 days it moves seven du.
translations.idiomatic: It stands 15½° strong east of the sun; direct at 1/12° per day, 7° in 84 days.

sentences.zh: 留，不行，三十六日而逆。

translations.literal: Stationary, not moving, thirty-six days, then retrograde.
translations.idiomatic: It stations for 36 days, then turns retrograde.

sentences.zh: 日行十七分之一，一百二日退六度。

translations.literal: Daily one part out of seventeen; in 102 days it retreats six du.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde at 1/17° per day, retreating 6° in 102 days.

sentences.zh: 又留三十六日。

translations.literal: Again stationary thirty-six days.
translations.idiomatic: It stations again for 36 days.

sentences.zh: 順，八十四日行七度，夕伏西方，日度余如初，與日合。

translations.literal: Direct: in 84 days it moves seven du; at dusk it hides in the west; day and du remainder as at first, and conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Direct motion 7° in 84 days, then hides in the west at dusk and reconjoins the sun.

sentences.zh: 一終三百七十八日，日餘八千九百六十五，行星十二度，度余九萬三千六百九十五。

translations.literal: One cycle: 378 days, day-remainder 8,965, planetary motion 12 du, du-remainder 93,695.
translations.idiomatic: One synodic cycle: 378 days with remainder 8,965, planetary travel 12° with residue 93,695.

sentences.zh: 金：初與日合，伏，四十一日，日余四萬九千六百八十四半，行五十一度，度余四萬九千六百八十四半，見西方。

translations.literal: Metal: at first conjunction with the sun, it hides forty-one days, day-remainder 49,684½, moving fifty-one du, du-remainder 49,684½; it appears in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Metal: hides 41 days with remainder 49,684½, advancing 51° with the same residue, then appears in the west.

sentences.zh: 去日十度。

translations.literal: It stands ten du from the sun.
translations.idiomatic: It stands 10° from the sun.

sentences.zh: 順，疾，日行一度十三分之三，九十一日行一百十二度而小遲。

translations.literal: Direct, fast: daily one du and three parts out of thirteen; in 91 days it moves 112 du, then slightly slow.
translations.idiomatic: Direct fast: 1° 3/13 per day, 112° in 91 days, then slightly slow.

sentences.zh: 日行一度十三分之二，九十一日行一百五度。

translations.literal: Daily one du and two parts out of thirteen; in 91 days it moves 105 du.
translations.idiomatic: Slightly slow: 1° 2/13 per day, 105° in 91 days.

sentences.zh: 又大遲。

translations.literal: Again greatly slow.
translations.idiomatic: Then very slow.

sentences.zh: 日行十五之十一，四十五日行三十三度。

translations.literal: Daily eleven parts out of fifteen; in 45 days it moves thirty-three du.
translations.idiomatic: Very slow: 11/15° per day, 33° in 45 days.

sentences.zh: 留，不行，八日而遲。

translations.literal: Stationary, not moving, eight days, then retrograde.
translations.idiomatic: It stations for 8 days, then turns retrograde.

sentences.zh: 日行三分之二，九日退六度，伏西方。

translations.literal: Daily two parts out of three; in nine days it retreats six du; it hides in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde at 2/3° per day, retreating 6° in 9 days, then hides in the west.

sentences.zh: 伏六日，退四度而與日合。

translations.literal: Hidden six days, retreating four du, then conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden 6 days while retreating 4°, then reconjoins the sun.

sentences.zh: 又六日退四度，晨見東方。

translations.literal: Again six days, retreating four du; at dawn it appears in the east.
translations.idiomatic: After another 6 days retreating 4°, it appears in the east at dawn.

sentences.zh: 逆，九日退六度。

translations.literal: Retrograde: in nine days it retreats six du.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde 6° in 9 days.

sentences.zh: 又留八日。

translations.literal: Again stationary eight days.
translations.idiomatic: It stations again for 8 days.

sentences.zh: 順，四十五日行三十三度。

translations.literal: Direct: in 45 days it moves thirty-three du.
translations.idiomatic: Direct motion 33° in 45 days.

sentences.zh: 小疾，九十一日行一百五度。

translations.literal: Slightly fast: in 91 days it moves 105 du.
translations.idiomatic: Slightly fast: 105° in 91 days.

sentences.zh: 大疾，九十一日行百一十二度，晨伏東方，日度余如初，與日合。

translations.literal: Greatly fast: in 91 days it moves 112 du; at dawn it hides in the east; day and du remainder as at first, and conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Fast direct 112° in 91 days, then hides in the east at dawn and reconjoins the sun.

sentences.zh: 一終五百八十三日，日余四萬八千六百一。

translations.literal: One cycle: 583 days, day-remainder 48,601.
translations.idiomatic: One synodic cycle: 583 days with remainder 48,601.

sentences.zh: 除一周，行星定二百一十八度，度余三萬六千七十六。

translations.literal: Remove one circuit; fixed planetary motion 218 du, du-remainder 36,076.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce by one circuit to net travel of 218° with residue 36,076.

sentences.zh: 一合二百九十一日，余四萬九千六百八十四半，行星如之。

translations.literal: One conjunction: 291 days, remainder 49,684½; planetary motion is the same.
translations.idiomatic: One inferior conjunction: 291 days with remainder 49,684½ and the same planetary arc.

sentences.zh: 水：初與日合，伏，十七日，日余七萬一千二百一十半，行三十四度，度余七萬一千二百一十半，見西方。

translations.literal: Water: at first conjunction with the sun, it hides seventeen days, day-remainder 71,210½, moving thirty-four du, du-remainder 71,210½; it appears in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury: at initial solar conjunction it disappears for 17 days with remainder 71,210½, advancing 34° with the same residue, then appears in the west.

sentences.zh: 去日十七度。

translations.literal: It stands seventeen du from the sun.
translations.idiomatic: It stands 17° from the sun.

sentences.zh: 順，疾，日行一度三分之一，十八日行二十四度而遲。

translations.literal: Direct, fast: daily one du and one part in three; in eighteen days it moves twenty-four du, then slow.
translations.idiomatic: Direct fast: 1° ⅓ per day, 24° in 18 days, then slower.

sentences.zh: 日行七分之五，七日行五度。

translations.literal: Daily five parts in seven; in seven days it moves five du.
translations.idiomatic: Slow direct: 5/7° per day, 5° in 7 days.

sentences.zh: 留，不行，四日，夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Stationary, not moving, four days; at dusk it hides in the west.
translations.idiomatic: It stations for 4 days, then hides in the west at dusk.

sentences.zh: 伏十一日，退六度，而與日合。

translations.literal: Hidden eleven days, retreating six du, then conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden 11 days while retreating 6°, then reconjoins the sun.

sentences.zh: 又十一日退六度，而晨見東方。

translations.literal: Again eleven days, retreating six du; at dawn it appears in the east.
translations.idiomatic: After another 11 days retreating 6°, it appears in the east at dawn.

sentences.zh: 留四日。

translations.literal: Stationary four days.
translations.idiomatic: It stations for 4 days.

sentences.zh: 順，遲，七日行五度。

translations.literal: Direct, slow: in seven days it moves five du.
translations.idiomatic: Direct slow: 5° in 7 days.

sentences.zh: 疾，十八日行二十四度，晨伏東方，日度余如初，與日合。

translations.literal: Fast: in eighteen days it moves twenty-four du; at dawn it hides in the east; day and du remainder as at first, and conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Fast direct 24° in 18 days, then hides in the east at dawn and reconjoins the sun with the initial day and degree residues.

sentences.zh: 一終一百一十五日，日余六萬六千七百二十五，行星如之。

translations.literal: One cycle: 115 days, day-remainder 66,725; planetary motion is the same.
translations.idiomatic: One synodic cycle: 115 days with remainder 66,725 and the same planetary arc.

sentences.zh: 一合五十七日，日余七萬一千二百一十半，行星亦如之。

translations.literal: One conjunction: 57 days, day-remainder 71,210½; planetary motion is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: One inferior conjunction: 57 days with remainder 71,210½ and the same planetary travel.

sentences.zh: 盈加縮減，十六除月行分，日法除盈縮分，以減度分，盈加縮減。

translations.literal: Surplus add, shrinkage subtract: divide the moon's motion parts by sixteen, divide surplus-shrinkage parts by the day divisor, use to reduce degree parts; surplus add, shrinkage subtract.
translations.idiomatic: Apply surplus by addition and shrinkage by subtraction: scale lunar motion parts by 1/16, convert excess-deficit parts through the day divisor to adjust degree parts, then add or subtract accordingly.

sentences.zh: 推卦：因雨水大小余，加大餘六，小餘三百一十九，小余滿三千六百四十八成日。

translations.literal: Method for pushing hexagrams: starting from the Rain Water large and small remainders, add six to the large remainder and three hundred nineteen to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills 3,648 it becomes a day.
translations.idiomatic: For hexagram rulership, take the Rain Water sexagenary line and add 6 to the day count and 319 to the fractional part; carry at 3,648 parts to the day.

sentences.zh: 日滿二十七日餘不足加減不加周虛。

translations.literal: When days fill twenty-seven and the remainder is insufficient for add-subtract, do not add the circuit void.
translations.idiomatic: Once the count reaches 27 days with a remainder too small to adjust, omit the circuit-void correction.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十年，承天奏上尚書：「今既改用《元嘉曆》，漏刻與先不同，宜應改革。

translations.literal: Yuanjia year 20, Chengtian submitted to the Minister over the Masters: "Now that we have switched to the 《Yuanjia Calendar》, the clepsydra marks differ from before and ought to be reformed.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 20, He Chengtian memorialized the Minister of Works: "Having adopted the Yuanjia Calendar, the water-clock graduations no longer match the old system and should be revised.

sentences.zh: 按《景初曆》春分日長，秋分日短，相承所用漏刻，冬至後晝漏率長於冬至前。

translations.literal: According to the 《Jingchu Calendar》, the spring-equinox day is long and the autumn-equinox day is short; the clepsydra marks used in succession have day clepsydra after the winter solstice consistently longer than before the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingchu Calendar fixes a long day at the spring equinox and a short one at the autumn equinox, yet the inherited clepsydra tables make daytime water longer after midwinter than before it.

sentences.zh: 且長短增減，進退無漸，非唯先法不精，亦各傳寫謬誤。

translations.literal: Moreover the increase and decrease of length lacks gradual transition—the advance and retreat have no gradation; not only is the earlier method imprecise, but each transmitted copy also contains errors.
translations.idiomatic: Day lengths rise and fall without smooth gradation, and the discrepancies are not due to the old formula alone—copyists have compounded the fault.

sentences.zh: 今二至二分，各據其正。

translations.literal: Now the two solstices and two equinoxes each rest on their proper values.
translations.idiomatic: Let the two solstices and two equinoxes each serve as their own fixed anchors.

sentences.zh: 則至之前後，無複差異。

translations.literal: Then before and after the solstices there will no longer be discrepancies.
translations.idiomatic: Then the intervals before and after each solstice will no longer disagree.

sentences.zh: 更增損舊刻，參以晷影，刪定為經，改用二十五箭。

translations.literal: Further adjust the old marks, consult the gnomon shadow, edit and fix as the standard, and switch to twenty-five arrow-tubes.
translations.idiomatic: Revise the old graduations against sundial shadows, establish the corrected norm, and adopt a twenty-five-tube clepsydra.

sentences.zh: 請台勒漏郎將考驗施用。

translations.literal: Request the Office clepsydra officer to examine and verify before use.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the palace clepsydra officer test and put the new scale into service.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court assented.

sentences.zh: 前世諸儒依圖緯雲，月行有九道。

translations.literal: Scholars of earlier ages, following the charts and weft texts, said the moon has nine paths.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars, relying on cosmological charts and apocrypha, held that the moon travels nine paths.

sentences.zh: 故畫作九規，更相交錯，檢其行次，遲疾換易，不得順度。

translations.literal: Therefore they drew nine circles intersecting and crossing; checking its sequence of motion, slow and fast alternated and changed—it could not follow a regular degree progression.
translations.idiomatic: They mapped nine interlocking circles, but the moon's observed pace refused to march evenly through such a scheme.

sentences.zh: 劉向論九道雲：「青道二出黃道東，白道二出黃道西，黑道二出北，赤道二出南。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's discussion of the nine paths says: "The green path, two exit east of the yellow path; the white path, two exit west of the yellow path; the black path, two exit north; the red path, two exit south.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang on the nine paths wrote: "Two green paths lie east of the yellow path, two white paths west of it, two black paths to the north, and two red paths to the south.

sentences.zh: 」又雲：「立春、春分，東從青道；

translations.literal: " He also said: "At Establishment of Spring and the spring equinox, it follows the green path from the east;
translations.idiomatic: He added: "From Establishment of Spring through the spring equinox the moon runs the green path in the east;

sentences.zh: 立夏、夏至，南從赤道。

translations.literal: At Establishment of Summer and the summer solstice, it follows the red path from the south.
translations.idiomatic: from Establishment of Summer through the summer solstice it follows the red path in the south.

sentences.zh: 秋白冬黑，各隨其方。

translations.literal: In autumn, white; in winter, black—each follows its direction.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn it takes the white path, in winter the black, each aligned with its season."

sentences.zh: 」按日行黃道，陽路也，月者陰精，不由陽路，故或出其外，或入其內，出入去黃道不得過六度。

translations.literal: " According to this—the sun travels the yellow path, the yang road; the moon is yin essence and does not follow the yang road, therefore sometimes it exits outside, sometimes enters inside; entering and exiting may not depart from the yellow path by more than six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In fact the sun keeps to the yellow path, the highway of yang; the moon, as yin essence, cannot stay on that road and so swings above or below it, never more than six degrees from the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 入十三日有奇而出，出亦十三日有奇而入，凡二十七日而一入一出矣。

translations.literal: After entering, in thirteen-odd days it exits; after exiting, in thirteen-odd days it enters—in all twenty-seven days for one entry and one exit.
translations.idiomatic: It takes a little over thirteen days to cross inward and the same to cross outward—one complete in-out cycle in twenty-seven days.

sentences.zh: 交于黃道之上，與日相掩，則蝕焉。

translations.literal: Where it crosses upon the yellow path and is masked by the sun, there is eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: When the crossing coincides with the sun on the ecliptic, an eclipse occurs.

sentences.zh: 漢世劉洪推檢月行，作陰陽曆法。

translations.literal: In Han times Liu Hong examined and checked lunar motion and made the yin-yang calendar method.
translations.idiomatic: In the Han, Liu Hong verified the moon's motion and devised the yin-yang calendar method.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十年，太祖使著作令史吳癸依洪法，制新術，令太史施用之。

translations.literal: Yuanjia year 20, the Founding Emperor had Recorder Clerk Wu Gui follow Hong's method, devise a new procedure, and order the Grand Clerk to apply it.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 20 Emperor Wen had archive clerk Wu Gui adapt Liu Hong's method into a new procedure and put it in use at the Astronomical Bureau.

sentences.zh: 《元嘉曆》月行陰陽法：

translations.literal: 《Yuanjia Calendar》 lunar motion yin-yang method:
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia Calendar: method for the moon's yin-yang motion:

sentences.zh: 陰陽曆損益率兼數

translations.literal: Yin-yang calendar excess-deficit rates and combined numbers
translations.idiomatic: Yin-yang calendar: excess-deficit rates and combined numbers

sentences.zh: 一日益十七初

translations.literal: Day 1: excess seventeen, initial.
translations.idiomatic: Day 1: excess rate +17, opening entry.

sentences.zh: 二日前限餘六百六十五微分一千七百三十八益十六十七

translations.literal: Day 2: front limit remainder 665, minute fraction 1,738, excess sixteen, combined number seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: Day 2: front-limit remainder 665, minute fraction 1,738, excess rate 16, combined number 17.

sentences.zh: 三日益十五三十三

translations.literal: Day 3: excess fifteen, combined number thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Day 3: excess rate +15, combined number 33.

sentences.zh: 四日益十二四十八

translations.literal: Day 4: excess twelve, combined number forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Day 4: excess rate +12, combined number 48.

sentences.zh: 五日益八六十

translations.literal: Day 5: excess eight, combined number sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Day 5: excess rate +8, combined number 60.

sentences.zh: 六日益四六十八

translations.literal: Day 6: excess four, combined number sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Day 6: excess rate +4, combined number 68.

sentences.zh: 七日益一七十二

translations.literal: Day 7: excess one, combined number seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: Day 7: excess rate +1, combined number 72.

translations.idiomatic: Day 8: deficit rate −2, combined number 73.
