translations.literal: Day 9: deficit six, combined number seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: Day 9: deficit rate −6, combined number 71.

sentences.zh: 十日損十六十五

translations.literal: Day 10: deficit ten, combined number sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Day 10: deficit rate −10, combined number 65.

sentences.zh: 十一日損十三五十五

translations.literal: Day 11: deficit thirteen, combined number fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Day 11: deficit rate −13, combined number 55.

sentences.zh: 十二日損十五四十二

translations.literal: Day 12: deficit fifteen, combined number forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Day 12: deficit rate −15, combined number 42.

sentences.zh: 十三日後限餘二千一十九微分一千七十九損十六二十七

translations.literal: Day 13: rear limit remainder 2,019, minute fraction 1,079, deficit sixteen, combined number twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Day 13: rear-limit remainder 2,019, minute fraction 1,079, deficit rate 16, combined number 27.

sentences.zh: 分日二千六百八十五半損十六大大者五千三百

translations.literal: Fraction day 2,685½, deficit sixteen; double-full value 5,300.
translations.idiomatic: Fraction-day row: 2,685½ parts, deficit rate 16, double-full combined number 5,300.

sentences.zh: 七十一分之三千四百七十二十一

translations.literal: Seventy-one parts: 3,470; twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Fraction 3,470/71 with combined number 21.

sentences.zh: 曆周，五萬五千五百一十七半。

translations.literal: Calendar cycle: 55,517½.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar cycle (li zhou): 55,517½.

sentences.zh: 差率，一萬一百九十。

translations.literal: Difference rate: 10,190.
translations.idiomatic: Difference rate (cha lü): 10,190.

sentences.zh: 微分法，一千八百七十八。

translations.literal: Minute-fraction divisor: 1,878.
translations.idiomatic: Minute-fraction divisor (weifen fa): 1,878.

sentences.zh: 推入陰陽曆術曰：以會月去入紀積月，餘以會數乘之，以所入紀交會差加之，周天乘之，滿微分法為大分，不盡為微分。

translations.literal: Method for pushing entry into the yin-yang calendar says: remove entry-into-era accumulated months by synodic months; multiply the remainder by the synodic number; add the conjunction difference of the era entered; multiply by the circuit of Heaven; when it fills the minute-fraction divisor it becomes large parts; what does not exhaust is minute fraction.
translations.idiomatic: To find yin-yang calendar entry: reduce accumulated months since era entry by synodic months, multiply the remainder by the synodic constant, add that era's conjunction offset, scale by the circuit of Heaven, and split the product at 1,878 into large and minute fractions.

sentences.zh: 大分滿周天去之，余不滿曆周者為入陽曆。

translations.literal: When large parts fill the circuit of Heaven remove them; if the remainder does not fill the calendar cycle, it is entry into the yang calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Remove full circuits of Heaven from the large parts; any remainder under the calendar cycle counts as yang-calendar entry.

sentences.zh: 余皆如月周得一日，算外，所求年正月合朔入曆也。

translations.literal: As for the remainder, each time it equals the lunar circuit obtain one day; outside the reckoning: this is the calendar entry at the first-month conjunction of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the residue by the lunar circuit for whole days; the result, exclusive in the count, is the yin-yang entry at the year's first-month new moon.

sentences.zh: 不盡為日餘。

translations.literal: What does not exhaust is day-remainder.
translations.idiomatic: The leftover is the day-fraction.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加二日，日餘一千三百三十一，微分一千五百九十八，如法成日，日滿十三去之，除日餘如分日。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add two days, day-remainder 1,331, minute fraction 1,598; when it fills the divisor it becomes a day; when days fill thirteen remove them; remove day-remainder as fraction-day.
translations.idiomatic: For each following month add 2 days plus remainder 1,331 and minute fraction 1,598, carrying at the divisor; drop full cycles of 13 days and apply the fraction-day reduction.

sentences.zh: 陰陽曆竟平入端，入曆在前限餘前，後限餘後者，月行中道。

translations.literal: When the yin-yang calendar cycle is complete and evenly enters the origin: if calendar entry is before the front limit remainder it is before; after the rear limit remainder it is after—the moon travels the middle path.
translations.idiomatic: At cycle turnover, if entry falls before the front-limit remainder or after the rear-limit remainder the moon is off the middle path; between those bounds it runs the central track.

sentences.zh: 求朔弦望定數：各置入遲疾曆盈縮定積分，以章歲乘之，差法除之，所得滿通法為大分。

translations.literal: To seek the fixed numbers for new moon, first quarter, and full moon: for each, set the slow-fast calendar surplus-shrinkage fixed accumulated fraction; multiply by rule years; divide by the difference method; what is obtained, when it fills the communication divisor, becomes large parts.
translations.idiomatic: To fix syzygy and quarter-moon times, take each slow-fast surplus-shrinkage corrected accumulator, multiply by rule years, divide by the difference divisor, and convert the quotient at the communication divisor into large parts.

sentences.zh: 不盡，以微分法乘之，如法為微分。

translations.literal: What does not exhaust—multiply by the minute-fraction divisor; when it fills the divisor it becomes minute fraction.
translations.idiomatic: For the remainder, scale by the minute-fraction divisor to obtain minute parts.

sentences.zh: 盈減縮加陰陽日餘，盈不足，以月周進退日而定，以定日餘乘損益兼數，為加時定數。

translations.literal: Surplus subtract, shrinkage add to the yin-yang day-remainder; where surplus is insufficient, advance or retreat the day to fix it; multiply the fixed day-remainder by the excess-deficit combined number: this is the fixed number for the hour of occurrence.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract surplus and add shrinkage to the yin-yang day-fraction, carrying days as needed, then multiply the fixed remainder by the table's combined number for the corrected hour mark.

sentences.zh: 推夜半入曆：以差率朔小餘，如微分法得一，以減入曆餘，不足，加月周而減之，卻一日，卻得分日，加其分，半微分為小分，即朔日夜半入歷歷餘小分也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing midnight calendar entry: the new-moon small remainder as difference rate, divided by the minute-fraction divisor obtaining one, subtract from calendar-entry remainder; if insufficient, add the lunar circuit and subtract; retreat one day, retreating obtains fraction-day, add its parts; half the minute fraction makes small fraction: this is the calendar-entry remainder and small fraction at midnight of the new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: For midnight entry, convert the conjunction fraction through the difference rate and minute-fraction divisor, subtract from the calendar remainder (borrowing a lunar circuit and one day if needed), add the fraction-day parts, and halve the minute fraction for the small-fraction term at new-moon midnight.

sentences.zh: 求次日，加一日，日餘十六，小分三百二十，小分如會從余，余滿月周去之，又加一日。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, add one day, day-remainder sixteen, small fraction three hundred twenty; when small fraction fills the divisor carry to remainder, when remainder fills the lunar circuit remove it and again add one day.
translations.idiomatic: For the following day add 1 day, remainder 16, and small fraction 320, carrying at the divisor and lunar circuit as required.

sentences.zh: 曆竟，下日余滿分日去之，于入曆初也。

translations.literal: When the calendar cycle is complete, if the lower day-remainder fills the fraction-day remove it—this is at calendar-entry origin.
translations.idiomatic: At cycle end, drop a full fraction-day from the day-remainder to reset calendar entry.

sentences.zh: 不滿分日者，值之，加餘一千二百九十四，小分七百八十九半，為入次曆。

translations.literal: If it does not fill the fraction-day and the value is hit, add remainder 1,294, small fraction 789½: this is entry into the next calendar.
translations.idiomatic: When the remainder falls short of a fraction-day at turnover, add 1,294 plus small fraction 789½ to enter the next cycle.

sentences.zh: 求夜半定日：以朔小余減入遲疾曆日餘，不足一日，卻得周日，加餘四百一十七，即月夜半入曆日及餘也。

translations.literal: To seek the fixed day at midnight: subtract the new-moon small remainder from the slow-fast calendar day-remainder entered; if insufficient for one day, retreat to obtain the circuit day, add remainder 417: this is the day and remainder of midnight calendar entry for the moon.
translations.idiomatic: For midnight correction, subtract the conjunction fraction from the entered slow-fast day-remainder; if that underflows a day, borrow the circuit day and add remainder 417 for the moon's midnight calendar entry.

sentences.zh: 以日餘乘損益率，盈縮積分，為定積分。

translations.literal: Multiply the day-remainder by the excess-deficit rate and the surplus-shrinkage accumulated fraction: this is the fixed accumulated fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the day-fraction by the excess-deficit rate and surplus-shrinkage accumulator to get the corrected accumulated fraction.

sentences.zh: 滿通法為大分，不盡以會月乘之，如法為小分，以盈加縮減入陰陽日餘，盈不足進退日而定也。

translations.literal: When it fills the communication divisor it becomes large parts; what does not exhaust—multiply by synodic months, divide by the divisor to obtain small parts; surplus add, shrinkage subtract from the yin-yang day-remainder; where surplus is insufficient, advance or retreat the day to fix it.
translations.idiomatic: Convert at the communication divisor, finish the tail with synodic months for small parts, then add surplus or subtract shrinkage from the yin-yang day-fraction, carrying days to fix the date.

sentences.zh: 以定日餘乘損益率，如月周，以損益兼數，為夜半定數。

translations.literal: Multiply the fixed day-remainder by the excess-deficit rate; as lunar circuit; by excess-deficit combined number: this is the midnight fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the fixed day-fraction by the excess-deficit rate, scale by the lunar circuit and combined number, for the corrected midnight mark.

sentences.zh: 求昏明數：以損益率乘所近節氣夜漏，二百而一為明，以減損益率為昏，而以損益夜半數為昏明定數也。

translations.literal: To seek dusk and dawn numbers: multiply the excess-deficit rate by the night clepsydra of the nearest solar term; one out of two hundred is dawn; subtract the excess-deficit rate for dusk; then by excess-deficit adjust the midnight number to obtain the dusk-and-dawn fixed numbers.
translations.idiomatic: For dawn and dusk corrections, take the nearest term's night water, allocate the excess-deficit rate in a 1:200 ratio for dawn and the balance for dusk, and shift the midnight value accordingly.

sentences.zh: 求月去黃道度：置加時若昏明定數，以十二除之為度，其餘三而一為少，不盡為強，二少弱也。

translations.literal: To seek the moon's departure from the yellow path in du: set the fixed number for the hour of occurrence or for dusk and dawn; divide by twelve for du; of the remainder, one out of three is shao; what does not exhaust is qiang; two shao make ruo.
translations.idiomatic: For lunar latitude, take the corrected hour, quarter, or dusk/dawn number, divide by 12 for whole degrees, then split the remainder into strong and weak parts in thirds.

sentences.zh: 所得為月去黃道度。

translations.literal: What is obtained is the moon's departure from the yellow path in du.
translations.idiomatic: The result is the moon's ecliptic latitude in degrees.

sentences.zh: 大明六年，南徐州從事史祖沖之上表曰：

translations.literal: Sixth year of Daming, Zu Chongzhi, registrar of South Xu Province, submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In Daming 6, Zu Chongzhi, aide to the governor of South Xu, submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 古曆疏舛，頗不精密，群氏糾紛，莫審其要。

translations.literal: The ancient calendars were coarse and erroneous, quite lacking in precision; various masters quarreled without discerning the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: The old calendars were loose and inaccurate, and rival schools disputed them without settling the core principles.

sentences.zh: 何承天所奏，意存改革，而置法簡略，今已乖遠。

translations.literal: What He Chengtian submitted intended reform, but the methods he established were simplified and sketchy, and they have now diverged far from accuracy.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian's proposal aimed at reform, yet the rules he set were too spare and have already drifted badly from the heavens.

sentences.zh: 以臣校之，三睹厥謬：日月所在，差覺三度；

translations.literal: By my verification, thrice I observed its errors: the positions of sun and moon differ by nearly three degrees;
translations.idiomatic: In three separate checks I found the same faults: the sun and moon are off by almost three degrees;

sentences.zh: 二至晷影，幾失一日；

translations.literal: At the two solstices the gnomon shadow nearly misses by a full day;
translations.idiomatic: solstice shadows err by nearly a whole day;

sentences.zh: 五星見伏，至差四旬，留逆進退，或移兩宿。

translations.literal: The five stars' appearances and disappearances miss by up to forty days; station, retrograde, advance and retreat sometimes shift by two lodges.
translations.idiomatic: planetary phases can be wrong by forty days, and stations, retrogrades, and reversals may wander two lodges off.

sentences.zh: 分至乖失，則節閏非正；

translations.literal: When the equinoxes and solstices go astray, the intercalary months and qi nodes are wrong;
translations.idiomatic: If the quarter and solstice points slip, intercalation and the qi nodes fall out of true;

sentences.zh: 宿度違天，則伺察無准。

translations.literal: When lodge degrees violate Heaven, observation has no standard.
translations.idiomatic: if lodge longitudes part from the sky, observation loses its measure.

sentences.zh: 臣生屬聖辰，逮在昌運，敢率愚瞽，更創新曆。

translations.literal: I was born in this sacred age, arriving in this flourishing fortune; I dare lead my dull vision to newly create a calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Born under a sage reign and a prosperous age, I venture despite my limited sight to draft a new calendar.

sentences.zh: 謹立改易之意有二，設法之情有三。

translations.literal: Respectfully I set forth two points in the intention to change, and three points in the disposition to establish methods.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully propose two grounds for reform and three principles for the new system.

sentences.zh: 改易者，其一，以舊法一章十九歲有七閏，閏數為多，經二百年，輒差一日。

translations.literal: Of the changes—first, the old method had seven intercalations in nineteen years, the intercalation count being too many; over two hundred years it would shift by one day.
translations.idiomatic: First change: the old rule of seven intercalations in nineteen years inserts too many leap months; in two centuries it slips a full day.

sentences.zh: 節閏既移，則應改法，曆紀屢遷，實由此條。

translations.literal: Once the qi and intercalation shift, the method ought to be changed; calendars have been repeatedly altered—truly from this cause.
translations.idiomatic: Once seasons and intercalation drift, the calendar must be revised—and that, I argue, is why systems have been rewritten again and again.

sentences.zh: 今改章法，三百九十一年有一百四十四閏。

translations.literal: Now changing the intercalation rule: in three hundred ninety-one years there are one hundred forty-four intercalations.
translations.idiomatic: My new intercalation rule yields 144 leap months in 391 years.

sentences.zh: 令卻合周、漢，則將來永用，無複差動。

translations.literal: Making it accord with Zhou and Han, then in future use forever, without further deviation.
translations.idiomatic: Aligned with Zhou and Han practice, it should serve indefinitely without further drift.

sentences.zh: 其二，以《堯典》雲：「日短星昴，以正仲冬。

translations.literal: Second, the 《Canon of Yao》 says: "The days are short and the star is Mao; thereby fix mid-winter."
translations.idiomatic: Second: the Canon of Yao says, "The days are short and the star is Mao—thereby fix mid-winter."

sentences.zh: 」以此推之，唐代冬至，日在今宿之左五十許度。

translations.literal: Inferring from this, at the Tang era midwinter the sun was at about fifty degrees to the left of today's lodge.
translations.idiomatic: From that line, at the Tang dynasty midwinter the sun stood some fifty degrees west of its present lodge.

sentences.zh: 漢代之初，即用秦曆，冬至日在牽牛六度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han they immediately used the Qin calendar; midwinter sun was at Ox six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: At the Han founding the Qin calendar placed midwinter at 6° in Ox.

sentences.zh: 漢武改立《太初曆》，冬至日在牛初。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu established the 《Taichu Calendar》; midwinter sun at the head of Ox.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's Taichu Calendar moved it to the start of Ox.

sentences.zh: 後漢《四分法》，冬至日在鬥二十二。

translations.literal: Later Han Four Elements method: midwinter sun at Dipper twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Han Quarter-Remainder system put it at Dipper 22.

sentences.zh: 晉時薑岌以月蝕檢日，知冬至在鬥十七。

translations.literal: In Jin times Jiang Ji used lunar eclipses to check the sun, knowing midwinter was at Dipper seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, Jiang Ji checked eclipses and found midwinter at Dipper 17.

sentences.zh: 今參以中星，課以蝕望，冬至之日，在鬥十一。

translations.literal: Now comparing with culminating stars and testing by eclipses and full moons, on midwinter day the sun is at Dipper eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing culminating stars with eclipse and full-moon tests, midwinter now falls at Dipper 11.

sentences.zh: 通而計之，未盈百載，所差二度。

translations.literal: Comprehensively reckoning, within not yet a full hundred years the discrepancy is two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Taken together, the shift is two degrees in less than a century.

sentences.zh: 舊法並令冬至日有定處，天數既差，則七曜宿度漸與曆舛。

translations.literal: The old methods all fixed the midwinter sun at a definite place; since the heavenly count has shifted, the seven luminaries' lodge degrees gradually diverge from the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Older systems pinned midwinter to a fixed longitude; as the sky moves, the seven luminaries steadily part from the calendar.

sentences.zh: 乖謬既著，輒應改制，僅合一時，莫能通遠，遷革不已，又由此條。

translations.literal: Once the error is evident, the system ought to be changed; it suited only one period and could not extend far—constant change also stems from this cause.
translations.idiomatic: Once the mismatch shows, reform is due; a fixed midwinter served one age but not the long term—and that too drove endless revisions.

sentences.zh: 今令冬至所在，歲歲微差，卻檢漢注，並皆審密，將來久用，無煩屢改。

translations.literal: Now making the midwinter position shift slightly each year, checking against Han annotations all are verified and precise; for long future use there will be no need for frequent changes.
translations.idiomatic: I would let midwinter advance slightly year by year; checked against Han observations it holds closely, and long use should not require repeated overhauls.

sentences.zh: 又設法者，其一，以子為辰首，位在正北，爻應初九，鬥氣之端，虛為北方，列宿之中，元氣肇初，宜在此次。

translations.literal: Of establishing methods—first, taking zi as the head of the chen order, position in due north, line corresponding to first nine, origin of Dipper qi, Emptiness as the northern direction, among the arrayed lodges—the primal qi begins here; it ought to be at this sequence.
translations.idiomatic: First principle of the new methods: take zi as the head of the earthly branches, due north, matching the first nine of the Changes—the Dipper's qi begins there, Emptiness marks the northern pivot among the lodges, and the primal breath rightly starts at this point.

sentences.zh: 前儒虞喜，備論其義。

translations.literal: The former scholar Yu Xi fully discussed its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier scholar Yu Xi set out that doctrine in full.

sentences.zh: 今曆上元日度，發自虛一。

translations.literal: The present calendar's superior-origin day-degree starts from Emptiness I.
translations.idiomatic: The present calendar's superior-origin solar longitude begins at Emptiness 1.

sentences.zh: 其二，以日辰之號，甲子為先，曆法設元，應在此歲。

translations.literal: Second, among the designations of day and chen, jiazi comes first; when a calendar method sets the origin, it should fall in this year.
translations.idiomatic: Second, jiazi leads the cycle of days and double-hours, so the calendar's epoch ought to fall in that year.

sentences.zh: 而黃帝以來，世代所用，凡十一曆，上元之歲，莫值此名。

translations.literal: Yet from the Yellow Emperor down, through the ages eleven calendar methods have been used, and none placed the superior-origin year on this designation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the Yellow Emperor onward, eleven calendars have been used across the ages, and not one placed the superior-origin year on jiazi.

sentences.zh: 今曆上元，歲在甲子。

translations.literal: The present calendar's superior origin falls in the year jiazi.
translations.idiomatic: The present calendar's superior origin is the jiazi year.

sentences.zh: 其三，以上元之歲，曆中眾條，並應以此為始，而《景初曆》交會遲疾，亦置紀差，裁合朔氣而已。

translations.literal: Third, with the superior-origin year all provisions in the calendar ought to start from it; yet the Jingchu Calendar, for conjunction and slow-fast motion, also sets era differences and only trims new-moon and qi alignment.
translations.idiomatic: Third, every calendar rule ought to begin from the superior-origin year; the Jingchu Calendar, however, offsets conjunction and lunar anomaly by era and trims only syzygy and solar-term alignment.

sentences.zh: 條序紛互，不及古意。

translations.literal: The sequence of provisions is tangled and mixed, falling short of the ancient intent.
translations.idiomatic: Its rules are jumbled and fall short of the classical intent.

sentences.zh: 今設法，日月五緯，交會遲疾，悉以上元歲首為始。

translations.literal: The present method makes sun, moon, five planets, conjunction, and slow-fast motion all start from the superior-origin year-head.
translations.idiomatic: The present method starts sun, moon, five planets, syzygy, and lunar anomaly all from the superior-origin year-head.

sentences.zh: 則合璧之曜，信而有征，連珠之暉，於是乎在，群流共源，實精古法。

translations.literal: Then the joined disc's brilliance has trustworthy evidence; the strung-pearls' radiance is thereby present; all streams share one source—truly refining the ancient method.
translations.idiomatic: Then the joined disc of sun and moon rests on solid evidence, the strung-pearl gathering of the five planets finds its place, and all streams share one source—truly refining the classical method.

sentences.zh: 若夫測以定形，據以實效，縣象著明，尺表之驗可推，動氣幽微，寸管之候不忒。

translations.literal: As for measuring to fix form and relying on real effect: the suspended images are clear and bright; gnomon-and-rule verification can be extrapolated; the moving qi is subtle, and clepsydra graduations are not wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against form and verified in practice, the suspended heavens stand clear; gnomon tests can be extrapolated, and even subtle qi and clepsydra graduations hold true.

sentences.zh: 今臣所立，易以取信。

translations.literal: What your subject has established is easy to trust.
translations.idiomatic: What I have established is easy to verify.

sentences.zh: 但深練始終，大存整密，革新變舊，有約有繁。

translations.literal: Only it deeply trains beginning and end, greatly preserves integral precision, innovates and changes the old, having both simplified and detailed parts.
translations.idiomatic: It works through every stage with full rigor, renews the old system, and mixes concise rules with detailed ones.

sentences.zh: 用約之條，理不自懼，用繁之意，顧非謬然。

translations.literal: In using simplified provisions I am not afraid on principle; in using detailed intent it is not, on consideration, mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: The simplified rules need not be feared on principle, and the detailed provisions are not arbitrary.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why so?

sentences.zh: 夫紀閏參差，數各有分，分之為體，非細不密。

translations.literal: Now era and intercalation are uneven; numbers each have their parts, and part-fractions as structure cannot be precise without fineness.
translations.idiomatic: Era cycles and intercalation are uneven, each constant has its proper fraction, and precision requires fine parts.

sentences.zh: 臣是用深惜毫釐，以全求妙之准，不辭積累，以成永定之制。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore deeply cherishes every hair's breadth to complete the standard of seeking refinement, and does not shrink from accumulation to achieve a permanently fixed system.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore guard every smallest fraction to reach an exact standard and do not shrink from cumulative detail to build a permanently fixed system.

sentences.zh: 非為思而莫悟，知而不改也，竊恐贊有然否，每崇遠而隨近；

translations.literal: It is not that I think yet fail to understand, or know yet fail to change; I privately fear that supporters have yea and nay, always honoring the distant while following the near;
translations.idiomatic: This is not from ignorance or obstinacy; I fear that in debate yea and nay alike exalt distant precedent while clinging to what is near at hand;

sentences.zh: 論有是非，或貴耳而遺目。

translations.literal: when arguments have right and wrong, some honor the ear and discard the eye.
translations.idiomatic: and that in judging right and wrong some trust hearsay over what the eye can see.

sentences.zh: 所以竭其管穴，俯洗同異之嫌，披心日月，仰希葵藿之照。

translations.literal: Therefore I exhaust my narrow views, bowing to wash away suspicion of difference, lay my heart open before sun and moon, and look up hoping for mallow-and-bean sunward illumination.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore lay out all I know, bowing to clear away suspicion of partiality, lay my heart open before sun and moon, and look up hoping for the sun's impartial light.

sentences.zh: 若臣所上，萬一可采，伏願頒宣群司，賜垂詳究，庶陳錙銖，少增盛典。

translations.literal: If what your subject submits has even one part in ten thousand worth adopting, I humbly wish it issued to all offices for detailed examination, hoping that a hairsbreadth's contribution may slightly augment the grand canon.
translations.idiomatic: If even a trace of what I submit may be adopted, I humbly ask that it be sent to all offices for full review, so that this tiny offering may add something to the grand canonical tradition.

sentences.zh: ○曆法

translations.literal: ○ Calendar Method
translations.idiomatic: ○ The Calendar Method

sentences.zh: 上元甲子至宋大明七年癸卯，五萬一千九百三十九年算外。

translations.literal: From the superior origin jiazi to the seventh year of Daming in Song, guimao, is 51,939 years, outside the reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: From the jiazi superior origin to Song Daming year 7 (guimao) is 51,939 years, exclusive in the count.

sentences.zh: 元法，五十九萬二千三百六十五。

translations.literal: Origin divisor: 592,365.
translations.idiomatic: The origin divisor (yuanfa): 592,365.

sentences.zh: 紀法，三萬九千四百九十一。

translations.literal: Era divisor: 39,491.
translations.idiomatic: The era divisor (jifa): 39,491.

sentences.zh: 章歲，三百九十一。

translations.literal: Rule years: 391.
translations.idiomatic: Rule years (zhang sui): 391.

sentences.zh: 章月，四千八百三十六。

translations.literal: Rule months: 4,836.
translations.idiomatic: Rule months (zhang yue): 4,836.

sentences.zh: 章閏，一百四十四。

translations.literal: Rule intercalations: 144.
translations.idiomatic: Rule intercalations (zhang run): 144.

sentences.zh: 閏法，十二。

translations.literal: Intercalation divisor: twelve.
translations.idiomatic: The intercalation divisor (runfa): twelve.

sentences.zh: 月法，十一萬六千三百二十一。

translations.literal: Month divisor: 116,321.
translations.idiomatic: The month divisor (yuefa): 116,321.

sentences.zh: 日法，三千九百三十九。

translations.literal: Day divisor: 3,939.
translations.idiomatic: The day divisor (rifa): 3,939.

sentences.zh: 餘數，二十萬七千四十四。

translations.literal: Remainder number: 207,044.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder number (yu shu): 207,044.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，九千五百八十九。

translations.literal: Year remainder: 9,589.
translations.idiomatic: The year remainder (sui yu): 9,589.

sentences.zh: 沒分，三百六十萬五千九百五十一。

translations.literal: Extinction parts: 3,605,951.
translations.idiomatic: The extinction parts (mo fen): 3,605,951.

sentences.zh: 沒法，五萬一千七百六十一。

translations.literal: Extinction divisor: 51,761.
translations.idiomatic: The extinction divisor (mofa): 51,761.

sentences.zh: 周天，一千四百四十二萬四千六百六十四。

translations.literal: Circumference of Heaven: 14,424,664.
translations.idiomatic: The celestial circumference (zhoutian): 14,424,664.

sentences.zh: 虛分，萬四百四十九。

translations.literal: Void parts: 10,449.
translations.idiomatic: The void parts (xu fen): 10,449.

sentences.zh: 行分法，二十三。

translations.literal: Motion-parts divisor: twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The motion-parts divisor (xingfen fa): twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 小分法，一千七百一十七。

translations.literal: Small-parts divisor: 1,717.
translations.idiomatic: The small-parts divisor (xiaofen fa): 1,717.

sentences.zh: 通周，七十二萬六千八百一十。

translations.literal: Communication circuit: 726,810.
translations.idiomatic: The communication circuit (tong zhou): 726,810.

sentences.zh: 會周，七十一萬七千七百七十七。

translations.literal: Conjunction circuit: 717,777.
translations.idiomatic: The conjunction circuit (hui zhou): 717,777.

sentences.zh: 通法，二萬六千三百七十七。

translations.literal: Communication divisor: 26,377.
translations.idiomatic: The communication divisor (tongfa): 26,377.

sentences.zh: 差率，三十九。

translations.literal: Difference rate: thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The difference rate (cha lü): thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 推朔術：置入上元年數，算外，以章月乘之，滿章歲為積月，不盡為閏餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing new moon: set the superior-origin year count, outside the reckoning; multiply by rule months; when it fills rule years it becomes accumulated months; what does not exhaust is intercalation remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To compute conjunction: from the superior-origin year count, multiply by rule months and divide by 391 for accumulated months; the remainder is the intercalation residue.

sentences.zh: 閏餘二百四十七以上，其年有閏。

translations.literal: If the intercalation remainder is 247 or more, that year has an intercalation.
translations.idiomatic: If the intercalation remainder is 247 or higher, the year receives a leap month.

sentences.zh: 以月法乘積月，滿日法為積日，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Multiply accumulated months by the month divisor; when it fills the day divisor it becomes accumulated days; what does not exhaust is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply accumulated months by 116,321 and divide by 3,939 for accumulated days; the remainder is the fractional day.

sentences.zh: 六旬去積日，不盡為大餘。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated days; what does not exhaust is the large remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce accumulated days modulo sixty for the day index.

sentences.zh: 大餘命以甲子，算外，所求年天正十一月朔也。

translations.literal: Name the large remainder from jiazi, outside the reckoning: this is the new moon of the eleventh month of Heaven's first month for the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Index the day from jiazi outward to obtain the civil eleventh-month new moon of the target year.

sentences.zh: 小餘千八百四十九以上，其月大。

translations.literal: If the small remainder is 1,849 or more, that month is long.
translations.idiomatic: If the fractional day is 1,849 parts or more, the month is long (30 days).

sentences.zh: 求次月，加大餘二十九，小餘二千九十，小余滿日法從大余，大余滿六旬去之，命如前，次月朔也。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add to the large remainder twenty-nine and to the small remainder 2,090; when the small remainder fills the day divisor carry to the large remainder; when the large remainder fills six decades remove it; name as before: the next month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add 29 days and 2,090 parts, carrying at 3,939 and reducing modulo sixty, then name the next new moon as before.

sentences.zh: 求弦望：加朔大餘七，小餘千五百七，小分一，小分滿四從小余，小余滿日法從大餘，命如前，上弦日也。

translations.literal: To seek first and full quarter: add to the new-moon large remainder seven and to the small remainder 1,507 and one small part; when small parts fill four carry to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the day divisor carry to the large remainder; name as before: the first-quarter day.
translations.idiomatic: For first quarter add 7 days, 1,507 parts, and 1 small part, carrying at 4 small parts, 3,939 parts, and sixty days, to name the upper-quarter date.

sentences.zh: 又加得望，又加得下弦，又加得後月朔也。

translations.literal: Add again to obtain full moon; add again to obtain last quarter; add again to obtain the next month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the step for full moon, last quarter, and the next month's new moon.

sentences.zh: 推閏術：以閏余減章歲，余滿閏法得一月，命以天正，算外，閏所在也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing intercalation: subtract intercalation remainder from rule years; when the remainder fills the intercalation divisor obtain one month; name from Heaven's first month, outside the reckoning: where the intercalation falls.
translations.idiomatic: For the leap month subtract the intercalation remainder from 391, divide by 12, and index from the civil first month outward.

sentences.zh: 閏有進退，以無中氣為正。

translations.literal: Intercalation may advance or retreat; the rule without a mid-term qi is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Leap placement may shift, but a month without a major solar term is the governing rule.

sentences.zh: 推二十四氣術：置入上元年數，算外，以餘數乘之，滿紀法為積日，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the twenty-four qi: set the superior-origin year count, outside the reckoning; multiply by the remainder number; when it fills the era divisor it becomes accumulated days; what does not exhaust is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: For the twenty-four qi, multiply years since the superior origin by 207,044 and divide by 39,491 for accumulated days; the remainder is the fractional day.

sentences.zh: 六旬去積日，不盡為大餘。

translations.literal: Remove six decades from accumulated days; what does not exhaust is the large remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce accumulated days modulo sixty for the day index.

sentences.zh: 大餘命以甲子，算外，天正十一月冬至日也。

translations.literal: Name the large remainder from jiazi, outside the reckoning: the Winter Solstice day of the eleventh month of Heaven's first month.
translations.idiomatic: Index from jiazi outward to obtain the civil eleventh-month Winter Solstice.

sentences.zh: 求次氣，加大餘十五，小餘八千六百二十六，小分五，小分滿六從小余，小余滿紀法從大餘，命如前，次氣日也。

translations.literal: To seek the next qi, add to the large remainder fifteen, to the small remainder 8,626, and five small parts; when small parts fill six carry to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the era divisor carry to the large remainder; name as before: the next qi's day.
translations.idiomatic: For each following qi add 15 days, 8,626 parts, and 5 small parts, carrying at 6 small parts and 39,491 parts.

sentences.zh: 求土用事：加冬至大餘二十七，小余萬五千五百二十八，季冬土用事日也。

translations.literal: To seek Earth taking reign: add to the Winter Solstice large remainder twenty-seven and to the small remainder 15,528: the day Earth takes reign in late winter.
translations.idiomatic: For Earth's reign in late winter add 27 days and 15,528 parts to the Winter Solstice index.

sentences.zh: 又加大餘九十一，小余萬二千二百七十，次土用事日也。

translations.literal: Again add to the large remainder ninety-one and to the small remainder 12,270: the next day Earth takes reign.
translations.idiomatic: Add another 91 days and 12,270 parts for the second Earth-reign day.

sentences.zh: 推沒術：以九十乘冬至小餘，以減沒分，滿沒法為日，不盡為日餘，命日以冬至，算外，沒日也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing extinction: multiply the Winter Solstice small remainder by ninety and subtract from extinction parts; when it fills the extinction divisor it becomes days; what does not exhaust is day-remainder; name the day from Winter Solstice, outside the reckoning: the extinction day.
translations.idiomatic: For extinction days subtract ninety times the Winter Solstice fraction from 3,605,951 and divide by 51,761, naming the date from Winter Solstice outward.

sentences.zh: 求次沒，加日六十九，日余三萬四千四百四十二，余滿沒法從日，次沒日也。

translations.literal: To seek the next extinction, add sixty-nine days and day-remainder 34,442; when the remainder fills the extinction divisor carry to the day: the next extinction day.
translations.idiomatic: For the next extinction add 69 days and 34,442 parts, carrying at 51,761 parts per day.

sentences.zh: 日餘盡為滅。

translations.literal: When the day-remainder is exhausted, it is a disappearance.
translations.idiomatic: When the fractional part reaches zero, that day is a disappearance (mie).

sentences.zh: 推日所在度術：以紀法乘朔積日為度實，周天去之，余滿紀法為積度，不盡為度餘，命以虛一，次宿除之，算外，天正十一月朔夜半日所在度也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the sun's lodge degree: multiply new-moon accumulated days by the era divisor for degree dividend; remove the circumference of Heaven; when the remainder fills the era divisor it becomes accumulated degrees; what does not exhaust is degree-remainder; name from Emptiness I and divide through the lodges, outside the reckoning: the sun's degree at midnight on the eleventh-month new moon of Heaven's first month.
translations.idiomatic: For solar longitude at the civil eleventh-month new moon, multiply accumulated days by 39,491, reduce modulo 14,424,664, index from Emptiness 1 through the lodges.

sentences.zh: 求次月，大月加度三十，小月加度二十九，入虛去度分。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, for a long month add thirty degrees and for a short month add twenty-nine; when entering Emptiness remove the degree parts.
translations.idiomatic: Each month add 30° for a long month or 29° for a short month, with the Emptiness-lodge reduction.

sentences.zh: 求行分，以小分法除度餘，所得為行分，不盡為小分。

translations.literal: To seek motion parts, divide degree-remainder by the small-parts divisor; what is obtained is motion parts; what does not exhaust is small parts.
translations.idiomatic: Divide degree remainder by 1,717 for motion parts; the tail is small parts.

sentences.zh: 小分滿法從行分，行分滿法從度。

translations.literal: When small parts fill the divisor carry to motion parts; when motion parts fill the divisor carry to degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Carry small parts into motion parts at 1,717 and motion parts into whole degrees at 23.

sentences.zh: 求次日，加一度。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, add one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Add 1° per day thereafter.

sentences.zh: 入虛去行分六，小分百四十七。

translations.literal: When entering Emptiness remove six motion parts and 147 small parts.
translations.idiomatic: When crossing Emptiness subtract 6 motion parts and 147 small parts.

sentences.zh: 推月所在度術：以朔小餘乘百二十四為度餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the moon's lodge degree: multiply the new-moon small remainder by 124 for degree-remainder.
translations.idiomatic: For lunar longitude multiply the conjunction fraction by 124 for degree remainder.

sentences.zh: 又以朔小餘乘八百六十為微分。

translations.literal: Again multiply the new-moon small remainder by 860 for minute parts.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the same fraction by 860 for minute parts.

sentences.zh: 微分滿月法從度余，度余滿紀法為度，以減朔夜半日所在，則月所在度。

translations.literal: When minute parts fill the month divisor carry to degree-remainder; when degree-remainder fills the era divisor it becomes degrees; subtract from the new-moon midnight sun position: then the moon's lodge degree.
translations.idiomatic: Carry minute parts at 116,321 and degree parts at 39,491, then subtract from midnight solar longitude to obtain the moon's position.

sentences.zh: 求次月，大月加度三十五，度余三萬一千八百三十四，微分七萬七千九百六十七，小月加度二十二，度余萬七千二百六十一，微分六萬三千七百三十六，入虛去度分也。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, for a long month add thirty-five degrees, degree-remainder 31,834, and minute parts 77,967; for a short month add twenty-two degrees, degree-remainder 17,261, and minute parts 63,736; when entering Emptiness remove the degree parts.
translations.idiomatic: Each long month add 35° plus 31,834 degree parts and 77,967 minute parts; each short month add 22° plus 17,261 and 63,736, with the Emptiness reduction.

sentences.zh: 遲疾曆：

sentences.zh: 推入遲疾曆術：以通法乘朔積日為通實，通周去之，余滿通法為日，不盡為日餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing entry into the slow-fast calendar: multiply new-moon accumulated days by the communication divisor for communication dividend; remove the communication circuit; when the remainder fills the communication divisor it becomes days; what does not exhaust is day-remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To enter the anomaly table multiply accumulated days by 26,377, reduce modulo 726,810, and split into days and day remainder.

sentences.zh: 命日算外，天正十一月朔夜半入曆日也。

translations.literal: Name the day, outside the reckoning: the calendar-entry day at midnight on the eleventh-month new moon of Heaven's first month.
translations.idiomatic: Index the day outward to obtain midnight calendar entry on the civil eleventh-month new moon.

sentences.zh: 求次月，大月加二日，小月加一日，日余皆萬一千七百四十六。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, for a long month add two days and for a short month add one day; the day-remainder is always 11,746.
translations.idiomatic: Each long month add 2 days and each short month 1 day, always with remainder 11,746.

sentences.zh: 曆滿二十七日，日余萬四千六百三十一，則去之。

translations.literal: When the calendar fills twenty-seven days and the day-remainder is 14,631, remove it.
translations.idiomatic: After 27 days with remainder 14,631, drop one full anomaly cycle.

sentences.zh: 求次日，加一日。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, add one day.
translations.idiomatic: Add one day per day thereafter.

sentences.zh: 求日所在定度：以夜半入曆日餘乘損益率，以損益盈縮積分，如差率而一，所得滿紀法為度，不盡為度餘，以盈加縮減平行度及餘為定度。

translations.literal: To seek the sun's fixed degree: multiply the midnight calendar-entry day-remainder by the excess-deficit rate and use it to decrease-increase the surplus-shrinkage accumulated parts; divide by the difference rate; what is obtained, when it fills the era divisor becomes degrees and what does not exhaust is degree-remainder; for surplus add and for shrinkage subtract from parallel degrees and remainder to make the fixed degree.
translations.idiomatic: For corrected solar longitude multiply the entered day-fraction by the table rate, adjust the surplus-shrinkage accumulator by the difference rate of 39, and add or subtract from mean longitude.

sentences.zh: 益之或滿法，損之或不足，以紀法進退。

translations.literal: If increasing fills the divisor, or decreasing is insufficient, advance or retreat by the era divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Borrow or carry at 39,491 parts when addition overflows or subtraction underflows.

sentences.zh: 求度行分如上法。

translations.literal: To seek degree motion parts, use the method above.
translations.idiomatic: Compute motion parts by the same carry rules.

sentences.zh: 求次日，如所入遲疾加之，虛去分如上法。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, add according to the slow-fast entry, and remove void parts by the method above.
translations.idiomatic: Advance daily by the entered anomaly increment and apply the Emptiness reduction as above.

sentences.zh: 推入陰陽曆術：置通實以會周去之，不滿交數三十五萬八千八百八十八半為朔入陽曆分，滿去之，為朔入陰曆分。

translations.literal: Method for pushing entry into the yin-yang calendar: set the communication dividend and remove the conjunction circuit; what does not fill the crossing number 358,888½ is the new-moon entry into the yang-calendar fraction; when full, remove it to obtain the new-moon entry into the yin-calendar fraction.
translations.idiomatic: To enter the yin-yang calendar, take the communication dividend, subtract the conjunction circuit (717,777), and read the remainder under crossing number 358,888½ as the yang-calendar fraction at new moon; subtract that amount again for the yin-calendar fraction.

sentences.zh: 各滿通法得一日，不盡為日餘，命日算外，天正十一月朔夜半入曆日也。

translations.literal: For each, when it fills the communication divisor obtain one day; what does not exhaust is the day-remainder; count the day, outside the reckoning: the calendar-entry day at midnight on the Heaven-standard eleventh-month new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Divide each fraction by the communication divisor (26,377) for whole days and a day-remainder, then name the date outside the count: midnight calendar entry on the first-month new moon of the civil year.

sentences.zh: 求次月，大月加二日，小月加一日，日余皆二萬七百七十九。

translations.literal: To seek the next month: for a long month add two days, for a short month add one day; the day-remainder in each case is 20,779.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add 2 days (long month) or 1 day (short month), always adding day-remainder 20,779.

sentences.zh: 曆滿十三日，日余萬五千九百八十七半則去之。

translations.literal: When the calendar fills thirteen days and the day-remainder is 15,987½, then remove it.
translations.idiomatic: When the sequence reaches 13 days with day-remainder 15,987½, drop that full yin-yang cycle.

sentences.zh: 陽竟入陰，陰竟入陽。

translations.literal: When yang is exhausted one enters yin; when yin is exhausted one enters yang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the yang half-cycle enter yin; at the end of the yin half-cycle enter yang.

sentences.zh: 求次日，加一日。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, add one day.
translations.idiomatic: For the next day add one day.

sentences.zh: 求朔望差，以二千二十九乘朔小余，滿三百三為日餘，不盡倍之為小分，則朔差數也。

translations.literal: To seek the new- and full-moon difference: multiply the new-moon small remainder by 2,029; when it fills 303 it becomes the day-remainder; what does not exhaust, double it for small parts: this is the new-moon difference number.
translations.idiomatic: For the syzygy correction, multiply the conjunction fraction by 2,029, divide by 303 for the day-remainder, and double the tail for small parts to obtain the new-moon difference.

sentences.zh: 加一十四日，日余二萬一百八十六，小分百二十五，小分滿六百六從日余，日余滿通法為日，即望差數也。

translations.literal: Add fourteen days, day-remainder 21,186, small parts 125; when small parts fill 606 carry to the day-remainder; when the day-remainder fills the communication divisor it becomes days: this is the full-moon difference number.
translations.idiomatic: Add 14 days, day-remainder 21,186, and small parts 125; carry at 606 small parts and 26,377 day-parts to obtain the full-moon difference.

sentences.zh: 又加之，後月朔也。

translations.literal: Add again for the next month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the addition for the following month's conjunction.

sentences.zh: 求合朔月食：置朔望夜半入陰陽曆日及餘，有半者去之，置小分三百三，以差數加之，小分滿六百六從日余，日余滿通法從日，日滿一曆去之。

translations.literal: To seek conjunction and lunar eclipse: set the new- and full-moon midnight yin-yang calendar days and remainders; where there is a half, remove it; set small parts 303; add the difference number; when small parts fill 606 carry to the day-remainder; when the day-remainder fills the communication divisor carry to days; when days fill one calendar cycle, remove it.
translations.idiomatic: For syzygy and eclipse timing, take midnight yin-yang calendar entry and remainder at new or full moon, drop halves, add difference number 303 in small parts, and carry through 606, 26,377, and the 13-day cycle as needed.

sentences.zh: 命日算外，則朔望加時入曆也。

translations.literal: Count the day, outside the reckoning: this is the calendar entry at the hour of new or full moon.
translations.idiomatic: Name the day outside the count to obtain the yin-yang calendar entry at the syzygy instant.

sentences.zh: 朔望加時入曆一日，日餘四千一百九十八，小分四百二十八以下，十二日，日余萬一千七百八十八，小分四百八十一以上，朔則交會，望則月食。

translations.literal: When the hour-of-syzygy calendar entry is one day with day-remainder 4,198 and small parts 428 or below, or twelve days with day-remainder 11,788 and small parts 481 or above, at new moon there is conjunction; at full moon there is lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If hour-entry is ≤1 day 4,198 parts 428, or ≥12 days 11,788 parts 481, new moon yields a solar-lunar conjunction and full moon yields a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 求合朔月食定大小餘：令差數日餘加夜半入遲疾曆余，日余滿通法從日，則朔望加時入曆也。

translations.literal: To seek the fixed large and small remainders for conjunction and lunar eclipse: let the difference-number day-remainder add to the midnight slow-fast calendar remainder; when the day-remainder fills the communication divisor carry to days: this is the calendar entry at the hour of new or full moon.
translations.idiomatic: To fix syzygy remainders, add the difference day-remainder to the midnight anomalistic entry, carrying at 26,377 parts, to obtain hour-of-syzygy calendar entry.

sentences.zh: 以入曆餘乘損益率，以損益盈縮積分，如差法而一，以盈減縮加本朔望小餘，為定小餘。

translations.literal: Multiply the calendar-entry remainder by the excess-deficit rate; use it to excess-deficit adjust the surplus-shrinkage accumulated fraction; divide by the difference method; for surplus subtract and for shrinkage add from the original new- and full-moon small remainder: this is the fixed small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the entered day-fraction by the table's excess-deficit rate, apply it to the surplus-shrinkage accumulator divided by the difference method (39), and adjust the base syzygy fraction—subtracting surplus and adding shrinkage.

sentences.zh: 益之或滿法，損之或不足，以日法進退日。

translations.literal: If increasing fills the divisor, or decreasing is insufficient, advance or retreat the day by the day divisor.
translations.idiomatic: On overflow or underflow in the correction, carry or borrow a day using the day divisor (3,939).

sentences.zh: 求合朔月食加時：以十二乘定小余，滿日法得一辰，命以子，算外，加時所在辰也。

translations.literal: To seek the hour of conjunction and lunar eclipse: multiply the fixed small remainder by twelve; when it fills the day divisor obtain one double-hour; count from zi, outside the reckoning: the double-hour where the event falls.
translations.idiomatic: For syzygy or eclipse time, multiply the corrected fraction by 12 and divide by 3,939 to name the double-hour from midnight.

sentences.zh: 有餘者四之，滿日法得一為少，二為半，三為太。

translations.literal: If there is remainder, quadruple it; when it fills the day divisor obtain one shao, two makes ban, three makes tai.
translations.idiomatic: Split any leftover into quarters of the day divisor for the shao, ban, and tai subdivisions.

sentences.zh: 又有餘者三之，滿日法得一為強，以強並少為少強，並半為半強，並太為太強。

translations.literal: If again there is remainder, triple it; when it fills the day divisor obtain one qiang; combine qiang with shao to make shao-qiang; combine with ban to make ban-qiang; combine with tai to make tai-qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Further triple the tail for strong (qiang) units and combine them with weak, half, or full subdivisions per the clepsydra notation.

sentences.zh: 得二者為少弱，以並太為一辰弱，以前辰名之。

translations.literal: Obtaining two qiang makes shao-ruo; combining with tai makes one chen-ruo; name it by the preceding double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: Two strongs collapse to a weak grade; adding to tai yields a weak double-hour mark named from the prior hour.

sentences.zh: 求月去日道度：置入陰陽曆餘乘損益率，如通法而一，以損益兼數為定，定數十二而一為度，不盡三而一，為少、半、太。

translations.literal: To seek the moon's degrees from the solar path: set the yin-yang calendar remainder, multiply by the excess-deficit rate, divide by the communication divisor; use it to excess-deficit adjust the combined number for the fixed value; divide the fixed number by twelve for degrees; what does not exhaust, divide by three for shao, ban, and tai.
translations.idiomatic: For lunar latitude, multiply the yin-yang remainder by the table rate, divide by 26,377, adjust the combined number, then convert to degrees at 12 parts per degree with third-degree shao, ban, and tai subdivisions.

sentences.zh: 又不盡者，一為強，二為少弱，則月去日道數也。

translations.literal: If again it does not exhaust, one makes qiang and two makes shao-ruo: this is the moon's degrees from the solar path.
translations.idiomatic: Any further remainder yields one strong unit or two for a weak grade—the final lunar distance from the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 陽曆在表，陰曆在裏。

translations.literal: The yang calendar is on the outside; the yin calendar is on the inside.
translations.idiomatic: Yang-calendar motion lies outside the solar path; yin-calendar motion inside it.

sentences.zh: 求昏明中星：各以度數加夜半日所在，則中星度也。

translations.literal: To seek the dusk and dawn culminating stars: for each add its degree number to the midnight solar position; this is the culminating-star degree.
translations.idiomatic: For dusk and dawn culminating stars, add each star's offset to the midnight solar longitude.

sentences.zh: 推五星術：置度實各以率去之，餘以減率，其餘如紀法而一，為入歲日，不盡為日餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the five planets: set the degree dividend and for each remove its rate; subtract the remainder from the rate; divide the remainder by the era divisor for days entered in the year; what does not exhaust is the day-remainder.
translations.idiomatic: For planetary conjunctions, divide each planet's degree dividend by its rate, subtract the remainder from the rate, and divide by the era divisor (39,491) for days and day-remainder entered in the year.

sentences.zh: 命以天正朔，算外，星合日。

translations.literal: Count from the Heaven-standard new moon, outside the reckoning: the day of stellar conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Name the date against the first-month new moon outside the count to obtain the conjunction day.

sentences.zh: 求星合度：以入歲日及餘從天正朔日積度及余，滿紀法從度，滿三百六十餘度分則去之，命以虛一，算外，星合所在度也。

translations.literal: To seek the degree of stellar conjunction: let the days and remainder entered in the year follow the accumulated degrees and remainder from the Heaven-standard new-moon day; when it fills the era divisor carry to degrees; when it fills 360 remove the degree parts; count from Emptiness I, outside the reckoning: the degree where the star conjoins.
translations.idiomatic: For conjunction longitude, add the year's entered days and parts to the new-moon accumulated longitude, carry at 39,491 and 360°, index from Emptiness 1, and read off the conjunction degree.

sentences.zh: 求星見日術：以伏日及餘，加星合日及余，余滿紀法從日，命如前，見日也。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the star's appearance day: add the hiding days and remainder to the star-conjunction day and remainder; when the remainder fills the era divisor carry to days; count as before: the appearance day.
translations.idiomatic: For first visibility, add the planet's hiding interval to the conjunction date and carry at 39,491 parts to name the appearance day.

sentences.zh: 求星見度術：以伏度及餘，加星合度及余，余滿紀法從度，入虛去度分，命如前，星見度也。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the star's appearance degree: add the hiding degrees and remainder to the star-conjunction degree and remainder; when the remainder fills the era divisor carry to degrees; on entering Emptiness remove the degree parts; count as before: the degree where the star appears.
translations.idiomatic: For appearance longitude, add the hiding arc to the conjunction degree, carry at 39,491, apply the Emptiness-lodge reduction, and index as before.

sentences.zh: 行五星法：以小分法除度餘，所得為行分，不盡為小分，及日加所行分滿法從度，留者因前，逆則減之，伏不盡度。

translations.literal: Method for the motion of the five planets: divide the degree-remainder by the small-parts divisor; what is obtained is the motion parts; what does not exhaust is small parts; each day add the motion parts and when they fill the divisor carry to degrees; if stationary continue from before; if retrograde subtract; during hiding do not complete degrees.
translations.idiomatic: For daily planetary motion, convert degree-remainders to motion parts via the small-parts divisor (1,717), add them day by day with carry, hold stations unchanged, subtract in retrograde, and omit degrees while hidden.

sentences.zh: 從行入虛，去行分六，小分百四十七；

translations.literal: In direct motion entering Emptiness, remove six motion parts and 147 small parts;
translations.idiomatic: When direct motion crosses Emptiness, subtract 6 motion parts and 147 small parts.

sentences.zh: 逆行出虛，則加之。

translations.literal: in retrograde motion leaving Emptiness, add them.
translations.idiomatic: When retrograde motion exits Emptiness, add them back.

sentences.zh: 木：初與日合，伏，十六日，余萬七千八百三十二，行二度，度余三萬七千五百四，晨見東方。

translations.idiomatic: It stations for 28 days.

sentences.zh: 又留二十八日。

sentences.zh: 日度余如初。

translations.literal: Day and degree remainders as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Day and degree remainders return to their initial values.

sentences.zh: 一終，三百九十八日，日余三萬五千六百六十四，行三十三度，度余二萬五千二百一十五。

sentences.zh: 火：初與日合，伏，七十二日，日餘六百八，行五十五度，度余二萬八千八百六十五，晨見東方。

translations.literal: Fire: at first conjunction with the sun, it hides seventy-two days, day-remainder 608, moving fifty-five degrees, degree-remainder 28,865; at dawn it appears in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Mars: hides 72 days with remainder 608, advancing 55° with residue 28,865, then appears in the east at dawn.

translations.idiomatic: Direct fast: 17 parts per day, 68° in 92 days.

translations.idiomatic: Slightly slow: 14 parts per day, 56° in 92 days.

translations.idiomatic: Retrograde: 6 parts per day, retreating 16° 16 parts in 64 days.

translations.idiomatic: Slightly fast: 14 parts per day for 92 days.

sentences.zh: 大疾，日行十七分，九十二日，夕伏西方，日度余如初。

translations.idiomatic: Fast direct: 17 parts per day for 92 days, then hides in the west at dusk with the same remainders as at first conjunction.

sentences.zh: 一終，七百八十日，日餘千二百一十六，行四百一十四度，度余三萬二百五十八。

translations.idiomatic: Reduce by one full circuit to net travel of 49° with residue 19,809.

sentences.zh: 土：初與日合，伏，十七日，日餘千三百七十八，行一度，度余萬九千三百三十三，晨見東方。

translations.idiomatic: Saturn: hides 17 days with remainder 1,378, advancing 1° with residue 19,333, then appears in the east at dawn.

sentences.zh: 行順，日行二分，八十四日，行七度七分。

translations.literal: Direct motion: daily two parts; in 84 days it moves seven degrees seven parts.
translations.idiomatic: Direct: 2 parts per day, 7° 7 parts in 84 days.

translations.idiomatic: It stations for 33 days.

translations.literal: Direct, fast: daily one degree five parts; in 92 days it moves 112 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Direct fast: 1° 5 parts per day, 112° in 92 days.

translations.literal: Slightly slow: daily one degree four parts; in 92 days it moves 108 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Slightly slow: 1° 4 parts per day, 108° in 92 days.

translations.literal: Greatly slow: daily seventeen parts; in 45 days it moves thirty-three degrees six parts.
translations.idiomatic: Very slow: 17 parts per day, 33° 6 parts in 45 days.

sentences.zh: 留九日。

translations.literal: Stationary nine days.
translations.idiomatic: It stations for 9 days.

sentences.zh: 遲，日行十六分，退六度六分。

translations.literal: Slow: daily sixteen parts; it retreats six degrees six parts.
translations.idiomatic: Slow retrograde: 16 parts per day, retreating 6° 6 parts.

sentences.zh: 夕伏西方。

translations.literal: It hides in the west at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: It hides in the west at dusk.

translations.literal: Hidden five days, retreating five degrees, then it conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden 5 days while retreating 5°, then reconjoins the sun.

translations.literal: Again five days, retreating five degrees; at dawn it appears in the east.
translations.idiomatic: After another 5 days retreating 5°, it appears in the east at dawn.

translations.idiomatic: It stations for 9 days.

translations.literal: Direct, slow: daily seventeen parts; forty-five days.
translations.idiomatic: Direct slow: 17 parts per day for 45 days.

translations.idiomatic: Slightly fast: 1° 4 parts per day for 92 days.

translations.idiomatic: Fast direct: 1° 5 parts per day for 92 days, then hides in the east at dawn with the same remainders as at first conjunction.

sentences.zh: 一終，五百八十三日，日余三萬六千七百六十一，行星如之。

translations.literal: One cycle: 583 days, day-remainder 36,761; planetary motion is the same.
translations.idiomatic: One synodic cycle: 583 days with remainder 36,761 and the same planetary arc.

sentences.zh: 除一周，定行二百十八度，度余二萬六千三百一十二。

translations.literal: Remove one circuit; fixed motion 218 degrees, degree-remainder 26,312.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce by one circuit to net travel of 218° with residue 26,312.

sentences.zh: 一合，二百九十一日，日余三萬八千一百二十六，行星亦如之。

translations.literal: One conjunction: 291 days, day-remainder 38,126; planetary motion is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: One inferior conjunction: 291 days with remainder 38,126 and the same planetary arc.

translations.idiomatic: Mercury: hides 14 days with remainder 37,115, advancing 30° with the same residue, then appears in the west at dusk.

translations.idiomatic: Direct fast: 1° 6 parts per day, 29° in 23 days.

translations.idiomatic: It stations for 2 days.

translations.idiomatic: Slow retrograde: 11 parts per day, retreating 22 parts in 2 days.

translations.literal: It hides in the west at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: It hides in the west at dusk.

translations.idiomatic: Hidden 8 days while retreating 8°, then reconjoins the sun.

translations.idiomatic: After another 8 days retreating 8°, it appears in the east at dawn.

translations.idiomatic: Retrograde: 11 parts per day for 2 days.

sentences.zh: 留二日。

translations.idiomatic: It stations for 2 days.

translations.literal: Direct, slow: daily twenty parts; eight days.
translations.idiomatic: Direct slow: 20 parts per day for 8 days.

sentences.zh: 疾，日行一度六分，二十三日，晨伏東方，日度余如初。

translations.idiomatic: Fast direct: 1° 6 parts per day for 23 days, then hides in the east at dawn with the same remainders as at first conjunction.

sentences.zh: 一終，百一十五日，日余三萬四千七百三十九，行星如之。

translations.literal: One cycle: 115 days, day-remainder 34,739; planetary motion is the same.
translations.idiomatic: One synodic cycle: 115 days with remainder 34,739 and the same planetary arc.

sentences.zh: 一合，五十七日，日余三萬七千一百一十五，行星亦如之。

translations.literal: One conjunction: fifty-seven days, day remainder thirty-seven thousand one hundred fifteen; planetary motion is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: One inferior conjunction: 57 days with remainder 37,115; planetary motion matches.

sentences.zh: 上元之歲，歲在甲子，天正甲子朔夜半冬至，日月五星，聚于虛度之初，陰陽遲疾，並自此始。

translations.literal: In the year of the superior origin, when the year was jiazi, at the heavenly first month jiazi new moon at midnight on the winter solstice, sun, moon, and five planets gathered at the start of the Void degree; yin-yang slow-fast cycles all begin from this point.
translations.idiomatic: At the superior origin, in the jiazi year, the first-month jiazi new moon fell at midnight on the winter solstice; sun, moon, and five planets stood at the start of the Void lodge, and yin-yang slow-fast reckoning all begin from that moment.

sentences.zh: 世祖下之有司，使內外博議，時人少解歷數，竟無異同之辨。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu ordered the relevant offices to have inner and outer officials debate broadly; at the time few understood calendrical numbers, and in the end there was no real disagreement or agreement distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu ordered the ministries to open debate inside and outside the court, but few then understood calendrical computation, and no clear consensus emerged.

sentences.zh: 唯太子旅賁中郎將戴法興議，以為：

translations.literal: Only the Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Crown Prince, Dai Faxing, submitted an opinion, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Only Dai Faxing, Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Crown Prince, offered a formal objection, saying:

sentences.zh: 三精數微，五緯會始，自非深推測，窮識晷變，豈能刊古革今，轉正圭宿。

translations.literal: The numbers of the three luminaries are subtle, and the five planets' conjunction beginning—unless one pushes deeply and measures exhaustively, fully knowing gnomon and seasonal change, how could one edit the ancient and reform the present, correcting the jade-standard lodges?
translations.idiomatic: The three luminaries' parameters are fine-grained and the five planets' conjunction epoch is delicate; without deep calculation and full mastery of gnomon and seasonal change, how could one revise antiquity, reform the present, and reset the jade-standard lodges?

sentences.zh: 案沖之所議，每有違舛，竊以愚見，隨事辨問。

translations.literal: Examining Chongzhi's proposals, each has errors and contradictions; I venture with my humble view to question them item by item.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing Zu Chongzhi's proposals, I find repeated errors; I shall therefore question each point in turn from my own limited understanding.

sentences.zh: 案沖之新推曆術，「今冬至所在，歲歲微差」。

translations.literal: Examining Chongzhi's newly proposed calendar method: "The winter solstice's position now shifts slightly every year."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi's new calendar holds that "the winter solstice moves slightly from year to year."

sentences.zh: 臣法興議：夫二至發斂，南北之極，日有恆度，而宿無改位。

translations.literal: Your subject Faxing submits: The two solstices mark expansion and contraction, the poles of north and south; the sun has a fixed degree, but lodges do not change position.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing replies: The solstices mark the turning points of seasonal expansion and contraction; the sun has fixed ecliptic measure, but the lodges do not shift their places.

sentences.zh: 古曆冬至，皆在建星。

translations.literal: In ancient calendars the winter solstice always fell in Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient calendars always placed the winter solstice in the Jian lodge.

sentences.zh: 戰國橫騖，史官喪紀，爰及漢初，格候莫審，後雜覘知在南斗二十二度，元和所用，即與古曆相符也。

translations.literal: In the Warring States era calendrical practice ran wild, historiographers lost proper reckoning; down to early Han, gnomon observations were uncertain; later mixed observation placed it at twenty-two degrees of Southern Dipper; the Yuanhe calendar used this, matching the ancient calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Warring States calendrics were chaotic and court historiography broke down; through early Han, gnomon readings were unreliable, until later observation fixed the solstice at Southern Dipper 22°—the Han Yuanhe calendar adopted that and matched the old reckoning.

sentences.zh: 逮至景初，而終無毫忒。

translations.literal: Down to the Jingchu era there was never the slightest error.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the Wei Jingchu calendar there was not the slightest discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 《書》雲：「日短星昴，以正仲冬。

translations.literal: The Documents say: "The days are short and the stars are the Pleiades—thus the mid-winter is fixed."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: "The days are short and the Pleiades culminate at dusk—thus mid-winter is fixed."

sentences.zh: 」直以月維四仲，則中宿常在衛陽，羲、和所以正時，取其萬世不易也。

translations.literal: Taking the four mid-season lodges by the moon's axis, the central lodges always stand in Weiyang; this is why Xi and He fixed the seasons, taking what would never change for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: If the four seasonal lodges are read by the moon's axis, their central stars always fall in the Weiyang quarter—the very reason Xi and He fixed time by what would never change for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 沖之以為唐代冬至日在今宿之左五十許度，遂虛加度分，空撤天路。

translations.literal: Chongzhi holds that in the Tang era the winter solstice stood some fifty degrees to the left of today's lodge, and therefore falsely added degrees and parts, emptying the celestial road.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi claims that at the Tang epoch the winter solstice stood some fifty degrees west of today's position, and on that basis he has added empty degrees and parts, dismantling the celestial road.

sentences.zh: 其置法所在，近違半次，則四十五年九月，率移一度。

translations.literal: Where his method is set, it nearly violates half a lodge; then every forty-five years and nine months the position shifts one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Where his method is anchored, it departs by nearly half a lodge; on his rate the solstice would shift one degree every forty-five years and nine months.

sentences.zh: 在《詩》「七月流火」，此夏正建申之時也。

translations.literal: In the Odes, "In the seventh month the Fire Star sets," marks the time when the Xia calendar takes shen as first month.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes' "In the seventh month the Fire Star sets" marks the month when the Xia calendar makes shen the first month.

sentences.zh: 「定之方中」，又小雪之節也。

translations.literal: "Ding is centered in the square" is again the Lesser Snow node.
translations.idiomatic: "Ding stands centered in the square" likewise belongs to the Lesser Snow node.

sentences.zh: 若冬至審差，則豳公火流，晷長一尺五寸，楚宮之作，晝漏五十三刻，此詭之甚也。

translations.literal: If the winter solstice were truly displaced, then in Duke of Bin's time the Fire Star would set, the gnomon shadow would be one chi five cun long, and when the Chu palace was built the day clepsydra would run fifty-three marks—an extreme absurdity.
translations.idiomatic: If the solstice were truly off by his amount, the Fire Star would set in Duke Bin's day, noon shadows would measure one chi five cun, and the Chu palace would have been built with a fifty-three-mark day clepsydra—an extreme absurdity.

sentences.zh: 仲尼曰：「丘聞之，火伏而後蟄者畢。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "I have heard that after the Fire Star sets, all hibernating creatures are finished."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "I have heard that after the Fire Star sets, every hibernating creature has finished its dormancy."

sentences.zh: 今火猶西流，司曆過也。

translations.literal: Now the Fire Star still moves westward—the calendar officer has gone too far.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Confucius' day the Fire Star was still moving westward—the calendar officer had fallen behind.

sentences.zh: 」就如沖之所誤，則星無定次，封有差方。

translations.literal: If it were as Chongzhi errs, then stars would have no fixed order and field-allotments would be displaced.
translations.idiomatic: If Zu Chongzhi were wrong in that way, stars would have no fixed order and regional field-allotments would be displaced.

sentences.zh: 名號之正，古今必殊，典誥之音，代不通軌，堯之開、閉，今成建、除。

translations.literal: Correct names of old and present must differ; the sounds of canonical edicts cannot match across ages; Yao's Opening and Closing become today's Establishment and Removal.
translations.idiomatic: The proper names of antiquity and the present would necessarily differ; the sounds of canonical edicts could not match across ages; Yao's Opening and Closing would become today's Establishment and Removal.

sentences.zh: 今之壽星，乃周之鶉尾，即時東壁，已非玄武，軫星頓屬蒼龍，誣天痛經，乃至於此。

translations.literal: Today's Longevity Star was Zhou's Chimei Tail; at present Eastern Wall is no longer Dark Warrior, and Chariot stars suddenly belong to Azure Dragon—distorting Heaven and violating the classics, even to this extent.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Longevity Star was Zhou's Chimei Tail; Eastern Wall is no longer Dark Warrior, and Chariot suddenly belongs to Azure Dragon—distorting Heaven and violating the classics to this degree.

sentences.zh: 沖之又改章法三百九十一年有一百四十四閏。

translations.literal: Chongzhi also changed the rule to three hundred ninety-one years with one hundred forty-four intercalations.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi also changed the intercalation rule to 391 years with 144 intercalations.

sentences.zh: 臣法興議：夫日有緩急，故鬥有闊狹，古人制章，立為中格，年積十九，常有七閏，晷或虛盈，此不可革。

translations.literal: Your subject Faxing submits: The sun has slow and fast motion, therefore the Dipper has wide and narrow openings; the ancients set the rule at a middle standard; over nineteen accumulated years there are always seven intercalations; the gnomon may be empty or full—this cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing replies: Because the sun's motion varies, the Dipper's opening varies in width; the ancients fixed the rule at a middle standard—over nineteen years there are always seven intercalations, and gnomon readings may run slightly long or short; this cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 沖之削閏壞章，倍減餘數，則一百三十九年二月，於四分之科，頓少一日；

translations.literal: Chongzhi cuts intercalations and breaks the rule, halving the remainder numbers; then in one hundred thirty-nine years and two months, under the Quarter-Remainder standard, one day is suddenly lost;
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi cuts intercalations and breaks the rule, halving the remainder numbers; then in 139 years and two months, on the Quarter-Remainder standard, one day is suddenly lost;

sentences.zh: 七千四百二十九年，輒失一閏。

translations.literal: in seven thousand four hundred twenty-nine years one intercalation is lost.
translations.idiomatic: in 7,429 years one intercalation is lost.

sentences.zh: 夫日少則先時，閏失則事悖。

translations.literal: If days are too few, the seasons come early; if intercalations are lost, affairs go wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Too few days make the seasons run early; lost intercalations make affairs fall out of step.

sentences.zh: 竊聞時以作事，事以厚生，以此乃生人之大本，歷數之所先，愚恐非沖之淺慮妄可穿鑿。

translations.literal: I have heard that seasons govern work, and work nourishes life—this is the great foundation of human existence and the first concern of calendrical reckoning; I fear this is not something Chongzhi's shallow thinking can arbitrarily rework.
translations.idiomatic: Seasons govern work, and work sustains life—that is the foundation of human existence and the first concern of calendrical science; I doubt Zu Chongzhi's shallow thinking can arbitrarily rework it.

sentences.zh: 沖之又命上元日度發自虛一，雲虛為北方列宿之中。

translations.literal: Chongzhi also set the superior-origin solar degree to begin from Void I, saying Void is the center of the northern lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi also set the superior-origin solar degree to begin at Void 1, claiming Void as the center of the northern lodges.

sentences.zh: 臣法興議：沖之既雲冬至歲差，又謂虛為北中，舍形責影，未足為迷。

translations.literal: Your subject Faxing submits: Chongzhi both claims winter-solstice precession and says Void is northern center; abandoning form and blaming the shadow is not enough to count as error.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing replies: Zu Chongzhi both claims solstice precession and calls Void the northern center; abandoning form for shadow alone is not yet proof of error.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 凡在天非日不明，居地以鬥而辨。

translations.literal: In Heaven nothing is clear without the sun; on earth one distinguishes by the Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In the sky nothing is clear without the sun; on earth one orients by the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 借令冬至在虛，則黃道彌遠，東北當為黃鐘之宮，室壁應屬玄枵之位，虛宿豈得複為北中乎？

translations.literal: Suppose the winter solstice were in Void: then the Yellow Path would be farther away; northeast ought to be the palace of Yellow Bell, and Room-Wall ought to belong to Dark Establishment—how could Void again be northern center?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose the solstice stood in Void: the ecliptic would lie farther out, northeast ought to be Yellow Bell's palace, and Room-Wall ought to fall in Dark Establishment—how could Void still be the northern center?

sentences.zh: 曲使分至屢遷，而星次不改，招搖易繩，而律呂仍往，則七政不以璣衡致齊，建時亦非攝提所紀，不知五行何居，六屬安托？

translations.literal: Forcing the four seasonal nodes to shift repeatedly while star orders do not change, changing the Dipper's cord while pitch-pipes stay as before—then the seven regulators would not be aligned by the armillary, and Establishment time would not be marked by Sagittarius; one would not know where the Five Phases dwell or where the six domains rest.
translations.idiomatic: Forcing the seasonal nodes to keep shifting while lodge order stays fixed, moving the Dipper cord while pitch-pipes remain unchanged—the seven regulators would not align by the armillary, Establishment time would not be marked by Sagittarius, and one would not know where the Five Phases or six domains belong.

sentences.zh: 沖之又令上元年在甲子。

translations.literal: Chongzhi also set the superior-origin year in jiazi.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi also set the superior-origin year in jiazi.

sentences.zh: 臣法興議：夫置元設紀，各有所尚，或據文於圖讖，或取效於當時。

translations.literal: Your subject Faxing submits: Setting the origin and establishing the era each follow different preferences—some rely on apocryphal texts, some take proof from their own time.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing replies: Setting the origin and establishing the era each follow different preferences—some rely on apocryphal texts, some take proof from their own time.

sentences.zh: 沖之雲，「群氏糾紛，莫審其會」。

translations.literal: Chongzhi says, "Schools dispute endlessly and none can verify the conjunction."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi says, "Schools dispute endlessly and none can verify the conjunction."

sentences.zh: 昔《黃帝》辛卯，日月不過；

translations.literal: Formerly the Yellow Emperor calendar used xinmao; sun and moon never exceeded;
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor calendar used xinmao; sun and moon never exceeded their bounds;

sentences.zh: 《顓頊》乙卯，四時不忒；

translations.literal: Zhuanxu used yimao; the four seasons were never off;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanxu used yimao; the four seasons were never off;

sentences.zh: 《景初》壬辰，晦無差光；

translations.literal: Jingchu used renchen; last days of months had no light error;
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu used renchen; last-day moons had no light error;

sentences.zh: 《元嘉》庚辰，朔無錯景，豈非承天者乎！

translations.literal: Yuanjia used gengchen; new moons had no shadow error—were these not calendars that matched Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia used gengchen; new moons had no shadow error—were these not Heaven-conforming calendars!

sentences.zh: 沖之苟存甲子，可謂為合以求天也。

translations.literal: If Chongzhi arbitrarily keeps jiazi, one may say he matched to seek Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If Zu Chongzhi arbitrarily keeps jiazi, one may say he forced a fit to seek Heaven's approval.

sentences.zh: 沖之又令日月五緯，交會遲疾，悉以上元為始。

translations.literal: Chongzhi also set sun, moon, and five planets' conjunctions, slow-fast motion, and all nodes to begin from the superior origin.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi also set sun, moon, and five-planet conjunctions, slow-fast motion, and all nodes to begin from the superior origin.

sentences.zh: 臣法興議：夫交會之元，則食既可求，遲疾之際，非凡夫所測。

translations.literal: Your subject Faxing submits: For the conjunction origin, eclipses can already be sought; for slow-fast junctures, this is not what ordinary men can measure.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing replies: From the conjunction origin eclipses can already be computed; slow-fast junctures are not what ordinary men can measure.

sentences.zh: 昔賈逵略見其差，劉洪觕著其術。

translations.literal: Formerly Jia Kui roughly saw their discrepancy; Liu Hong crudely set out their method.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui roughly saw their discrepancy; Liu Hong crudely set out their method.

sentences.zh: 至於疏密之數，莫究其極。

translations.literal: As for the numbers of density and fineness, none reached the ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: As for the fine and coarse numbers, none reached the ultimate.

sentences.zh: 且五緯所居，有時盈縮，即如歲星在軫，見超七辰，術家既追算以會今，則往之與來，斷可知矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the five planets' positions sometimes expand and contract; just as when Jupiter is in Chariot it appears seven lodges ahead, calendrists already trace calculation to match the present—then past and future can surely be known.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the five planets' positions sometimes expand and contract; when Jupiter is in Chariot it appears seven lodges ahead, and calendrists already trace calculation to match the present—past and future can surely be known.

sentences.zh: 《景初》所以紀首置差，《元嘉》兼又各設後元者，其並省功於實用，不虛推以為煩也。

translations.literal: Why Jingchu placed an initial discrepancy at the era-head and Yuanjia also set separate later origins was to save labor in practical use, not to push emptily and make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu placed an initial discrepancy at the era-head and Yuanjia set separate later origins to save labor in practical use, not to push emptily and make trouble.

sentences.zh: 沖之既違天于改易，又設法以遂情，愚謂此治曆之大過也。

translations.literal: Chongzhi both violates Heaven in reform and sets methods to suit his wishes; I deem this a great fault in governing the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi both violates Heaven in reform and sets methods to suit his wishes; I deem this a great fault in governing the calendar.

sentences.zh: 臣法興議：日有八行，各成一道，月有一道，離為九行，左交右疾，倍半相違，其一終之理，日數宜同。

translations.literal: Your subject Faxing submits: The sun has eight motions, each forming one path; the moon has one path, divided into nine motions; left is crossing, right is fast, double and half mutually diverge; for one cycle's principle the day-count ought to be the same.
