translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing replies: The sun has eight motions, each forming one path; the moon has one path divided into nine; crossing left and fast right, double and half mutually diverge—for one complete cycle the day-count ought to be the same.

sentences.zh: 沖之通周與會周相覺九千四十，其陰陽七十九周有奇，遲疾不及一匝。

translations.literal: Chongzhi's communication cycle and conjunction cycle differ by nine thousand forty; his yin-yang seventy-nine cycles have a fraction, slow-fast not reaching one circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi's communication cycle and conjunction cycle differ by 9,040; his yin-yang seventy-nine cycles have a fraction, slow-fast falling short of one circuit.

sentences.zh: 此則當縮反盈，應損更益。

translations.literal: This means where there should be shrinkage there is instead surplus, where there should be decrease there is instead increase.
translations.idiomatic: This means where there should be shrinkage there is surplus, where there should be decrease there is increase.

sentences.zh: 沖之隨法興所難辯折之曰：

translations.literal: Chongzhi followed Faxing's objections and rebutted them, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi answered Dai Faxing's objections point by point, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣少銳愚尚，專功數術，搜練古今，博采沈奧，唐篇夏典，莫不揆量，周正漢朔，鹹加該驗。

translations.literal: From youth I was dull but eager, specializing in numerical methods, searching and refining ancient and modern, broadly collecting hidden depths; Tang documents and Xia canons I have all measured; Zhou first month and Han new moon I have all tested.
translations.idiomatic: From youth I was dull but eager, specializing in numerical methods, searching ancient and modern sources and collecting hidden depths; Tang documents and Xia canons I have all measured; Zhou first month and Han new moon I have all tested.

sentences.zh: 罄策籌之思，究疏密之辨。

translations.literal: I exhausted the thought of counting-rods and pursued the distinction of coarse and fine.
translations.idiomatic: I exhausted counting-rod analysis and pursued the distinction of coarse and fine.

sentences.zh: 至若立圓舊誤，張衡述而弗改；

translations.literal: As for the old error in establishing the circle, Zhang Heng described it and did not change it;
translations.idiomatic: As for the old error in establishing the circle, Zhang Heng described it and did not change it;

sentences.zh: 漢時斛銘，劉歆詭謬其數，此則算氏之劇疵也。

translations.literal: the Han-era hu inscription, Liu Xin falsified its numbers—this is a gross flaw of the calculators.
translations.idiomatic: the Han-era hu inscription, Liu Xin falsified its numbers—this is a gross flaw of the calculators.

sentences.zh: 《乾象》之弦望定數，《景初》之交度周日，匪謂測候不精，遂乃乘除翻謬，斯又曆家之甚失也。

translations.literal: Qianxiang's fixed numbers for quarter and full moon, Jingchu's crossing-degree circuit day—this was not because observation was imprecise, but because multiplication and division were reversed in error; this again is a grave lapse of calendrists.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxiang's fixed numbers for quarter and full moon, Jingchu's crossing-degree circuit day—this was not because observation was imprecise, but because multiplication and division were reversed in error; this again is a grave lapse of calendrists.

sentences.zh: 及鄭玄、闞澤、王蕃、劉徽，並綜數藝，而每多疏舛。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan, Kan Ze, Wang Fan, and Liu Hui all combined numerical arts, yet each had many coarse errors.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan, Kan Ze, Wang Fan, and Liu Hui all combined numerical arts, yet each had many coarse errors.

sentences.zh: 臣昔以暇日，撰正眾謬，理據炳然，易可詳密，此臣以俯信偏識，不虛推古人者也。

translations.literal: Formerly in leisure days I corrected common errors; the reasoning is clear and can be examined in detail—this is how I rely on partial knowledge and do not push the ancients emptily.
translations.idiomatic: In leisure days I corrected common errors; the reasoning is clear and can be examined in detail—this is how I rely on partial knowledge and do not push the ancients emptily.

sentences.zh: 按何承天曆，二至先天，閏移一月，五星見伏，或違四旬，列差妄設，當益反損，皆前術之乖遠，臣曆所改定也。

translations.literal: Examining He Chengtian's calendar: the two solstices preceded Heaven, intercalation shifted a month, five planets' visibility sometimes violated four ten-day periods, listed discrepancies were falsely set, where increase was needed decrease was applied—all distant errors of earlier methods that my calendar has corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Examining He Chengtian's calendar: the two solstices preceded Heaven, intercalation shifted a month, five-planet visibility sometimes missed by four ten-day periods, listed discrepancies were falsely set, where increase was needed decrease was applied—all distant errors of earlier methods that my calendar has corrected.

sentences.zh: 既沿波以討其源，刪滯以暢其要，能使躔次上通，晷管下合，反以譏詆，不其惜乎！

translations.literal: Having followed the wave to seek the source and removed stagnation to clarify the essentials, it can make lodge order connect above and gnomon and clepsydra match below—yet you turn to ridicule; is this not regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: Having traced the stream to its source and removed stagnation to clarify the essentials, it can make lodge order connect above and gnomon and clepsydra match below—yet you turn to ridicule; is this not regrettable!

sentences.zh: 尋法興所議六條，並不造理難之關楗。

translations.literal: Examining Faxing's six objections, none reaches the key of rational difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Dai Faxing's six objections, none reaches the key of rational difficulty.

sentences.zh: 謹陳其目。

translations.literal: I respectfully set out the items.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully set out the items.

sentences.zh: 其一，日度歲差，前法所略，臣據經史辨正此數，而法興設難，徵引《詩》《書》，三事皆謬。

translations.literal: First, solar-degree annual precession: earlier methods omitted this; I corrected the number according to classics and history, yet Faxing objects, citing the Odes and Documents—on all three points he is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: First, solar-degree annual precession: earlier methods omitted this; I corrected the number according to classics and history, yet Dai Faxing objects, citing the Odes and Documents—on all three points he is wrong.

sentences.zh: 其二，臣校晷景，改舊章法，法興立難，不能有詰，直雲「恐非淺慮，所可穿鑿」。

translations.literal: Second, I corrected gnomon shadows and changed the old rule; Faxing objects but cannot rebut, saying only "I fear this is not shallow thinking that can be reworked."
translations.idiomatic: Second, I corrected gnomon shadows and changed the old rule; Dai Faxing objects but cannot rebut, saying only "I fear this is not shallow thinking that can be reworked."

sentences.zh: 其三，次改方移，臣無此法，求術意誤，橫生嫌貶。

translations.literal: Third, changing lodge position—this method I do not have; he misread the intent of the method and groundlessly slandered it.
translations.idiomatic: Third, changing lodge position—this method I do not have; he misread the intent of the method and groundlessly slandered it.

sentences.zh: 其四，曆上元年甲子，術體明整，則苟合可疑。

translations.literal: Fourth, the superior-origin year jiazi—the method's form is clear and whole, yet he calls a forced fit suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the superior-origin year jiazi—the method's form is clear and whole, yet he calls a forced fit suspicious.

sentences.zh: 其五，臣其曆七曜，鹹始上元，無隙可乘，複雲「非凡夫所測」。

translations.literal: Fifth, my calendar's seven luminaries all begin from the superior origin with no gap to exploit, yet he again says "not what ordinary men can measure."
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, my calendar's seven luminaries all begin from the superior origin with no gap to exploit, yet he again says "not what ordinary men can measure."

sentences.zh: 其六，遲疾陰陽，法興所未解，誤謂兩率日數宜同。

translations.literal: Sixth, slow-fast yin-yang—what Faxing has not understood he wrongly says the two rates' day-counts ought to be the same.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, slow-fast yin-yang—what Dai Faxing has not understood he wrongly says the two rates' day-counts ought to be the same.

sentences.zh: 凡此眾條，或援謬目譏，或空加抑絕，未聞折正之談，厭心之論也。

translations.literal: Of all these items, some cite false points to ridicule, some suppress emptily; I have not heard correcting discussion, only arguments that weary the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Of all these items, some cite false points to ridicule, some suppress emptily; I have not heard correcting discussion, only arguments that weary the heart.

sentences.zh: 謹隨詰洗釋，依源征對。

translations.literal: I respectfully follow each question to clarify, tracing the source and matching evidence.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully follow each question to clarify, tracing the source and matching evidence.

sentences.zh: 仰照天暉，敢罄管穴。

translations.literal: Looking up to Heaven's brightness, I dare exhaust my narrow understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up to Heaven's brightness, I dare exhaust my narrow understanding.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「夫二至發斂，南北之極，日有恆度，而宿無改位。

translations.literal: Faxing submitted: "The two solstices mark expansion and contraction, the poles of north and south; the sun has a fixed degree, but lodges do not change position.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing submitted: "The solstices mark expansion and contraction, the poles of north and south; the sun has fixed measure, but lodges do not change position.

sentences.zh: 故古曆冬至，皆在建星」。

translations.literal: Therefore in ancient calendars the winter solstice always fell in Jianxing."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore ancient calendars always placed the winter solstice in the Jian lodge."

sentences.zh: 沖之曰：周漢之際，疇人喪業，曲技競設，圖緯實繁，或借號帝王以崇其大，或假名聖賢以神其說。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said: Between Zhou and Han, calendrists lost their profession; crooked arts competed, apocryphal charts flourished; some borrowed imperial titles to magnify themselves, some borrowed sage names to make their doctrines divine.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi said: Between Zhou and Han, calendrists lost their profession; crooked arts competed and apocryphal charts flourished; some borrowed imperial titles to magnify themselves, some borrowed sage names to make their doctrines divine.

sentences.zh: 是以讖記多虛，桓譚知其矯妄；

translations.literal: Therefore apocryphal records are mostly empty; Huan Tan knew their falsity;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore apocryphal records are mostly empty; Huan Tan knew their falsity;

sentences.zh: 古曆舛雜，杜預疑其非直。

translations.literal: ancient calendars were mixed and wrong; Du Yu doubted they were not straight.
translations.idiomatic: ancient calendars were mixed and wrong; Du Yu doubted they were not straight.

sentences.zh: 按《五紀論》黃帝曆有四法，顓頊、夏、周並有二術，詭異紛然，則孰識其正，此古曆可疑之據一也。

translations.literal: Examining the Five-Era Treatise, the Yellow Emperor calendar had four methods; Zhuanxu, Xia, and Zhou each had two methods—strange and conflicting; then who knows which is correct? This is the first ground for doubting ancient calendars.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Five-Era Treatise, the Yellow Emperor calendar had four methods; Zhuanxu, Xia, and Zhou each had two—strange and conflicting; then who knows which is correct? This is the first ground for doubting ancient calendars.

sentences.zh: 夏曆七曜西行，特違眾法，劉向以為後人所造，此可疑之據二也。

translations.literal: The Xia calendar made the seven luminaries move westward, specially violating common methods; Liu Xiang held it was made by later men—this is the second ground for doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia calendar made the seven luminators move westward, specially violating common methods; Liu Xiang held it was made by later men—this is the second ground for doubt.

sentences.zh: 殷曆日法九百四十，而《乾鑿度》雲殷曆以八十一為日法。

translations.literal: The Yin calendar's day divisor was nine hundred forty, yet the Qianzao Du says the Yin calendar used eighty-one as day divisor.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin calendar's day divisor was 940, yet the Qianzao Du says the Yin calendar used 81 as day divisor.

sentences.zh: 若《易緯》非差，殷曆必妄，此可疑之據三也。

translations.literal: If the Changes Apocrypha is not wrong, the Yin calendar must be false—this is the third ground for doubt.
translations.idiomatic: If the Changes Apocrypha is not wrong, the Yin calendar must be false—this is the third ground for doubt.

sentences.zh: 《顓頊》曆元，歲在乙卯，而《命曆序》雲：「此術設元，歲在甲寅。

translations.literal: The Zhuanxu calendar's origin year was in yimao, yet the Mingli Xu says: "This method sets the origin year in jiayin."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuanxu calendar's origin year was in yimao, yet the Mingli Xu says: "This method sets the origin year in jiayin."

sentences.zh: 」此可疑之據四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth ground for doubt.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth ground for doubt.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》書食有日朔者凡二十六，其所據曆，非周則魯。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals record eclipses with day and new moon twenty-six times in all; the calendar used was either Zhou or Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals record twenty-six eclipses with day and new moon; the calendar used was either Zhou or Lu.

sentences.zh: 以周曆考之，檢其朔日，失二十五，魯曆校之，又失十三。

translations.literal: Testing by the Zhou calendar, checking new-moon days, twenty-five fail; testing by the Lu calendar, thirteen fail again.
translations.idiomatic: Testing by the Zhou calendar, checking new-moon days, twenty-five fail; testing by the Lu calendar, thirteen fail again.

sentences.zh: 二曆並乖，則必有一偽，此可疑之據五也。

translations.literal: Both calendars are wrong, so one must be false—this is the fifth ground for doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Both calendars are wrong, so one must be false—this is the fifth ground for doubt.

sentences.zh: 古之六術，並同《四分》，《四分》之法，久則後天。

translations.literal: The six ancient methods all match the Quarter-Remainder; the Quarter-Remainder method, over long time, lags Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The six ancient methods all match the Quarter-Remainder; the Quarter-Remainder method, over long time, lags Heaven.

sentences.zh: 以食檢之，經三百年，輒差一日。

translations.literal: Testing by eclipses, over three hundred years it suddenly misses one day.
translations.idiomatic: Testing by eclipses, over three hundred years it suddenly misses one day.

sentences.zh: 古曆課今，其甚疏者，朔後天過二日有餘。

translations.literal: Testing ancient calendars against the present, where most coarse, new moons lag Heaven by more than two days.
translations.idiomatic: Testing ancient calendars against the present, where most coarse, new moons lag Heaven by more than two days.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，古術之作，皆在漢初週末，理不得遠。

translations.literal: Pushing from this, the making of ancient methods was all in early Han and late Zhou—it cannot logically be far earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Pushing from this, ancient methods were all made in early Han and late Zhou—it cannot logically be far earlier.

sentences.zh: 且卻校《春秋》，朔並先天，此則非三代以前之明征矣，此可疑之據六也。

translations.literal: Moreover testing against the Spring and Autumn Annals, new moons all precede Heaven—this is not clear proof from before the Three Dynasties; this is the sixth ground for doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover testing against the Spring and Autumn Annals, new moons all precede Heaven—this is not clear proof from before the Three Dynasties; this is the sixth ground for doubt.

sentences.zh: 尋《律曆志》，前漢冬至日在鬥牛之際，度在建星，其勢相鄰，自非帝者有造，則儀漏或闕，豈能窮密盡微，纖毫不失。

translations.literal: Examining the Treatise on Pitch-pipes and Calendars, in Former Han the winter solstice stood at the juncture of Dipper and Ox, the degree in Jianxing—the positions are adjacent; unless the emperor made it, instruments and clepsydra were perhaps lacking—how could it be exhaustively fine without the slightest loss.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Treatise on Pitch-pipes and Calendars, in Former Han the winter solstice stood at the juncture of Dipper and Ox, the degree in Jian—the positions are adjacent; unless the emperor made it, instruments and clepsydra were perhaps lacking—how could it be exhaustively fine without the slightest loss.

sentences.zh: 建星之說，未足證矣。

translations.literal: The Jianxing theory is not sufficient proof.
translations.idiomatic: The Jianxing theory is not sufficient proof.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「戰國橫騖，史官喪紀，爰及漢初，格候莫審，後雜覘知在南斗二十二度，元和所用，即與古曆相符也。

translations.literal: Faxing submitted: "In the Warring States era calendrical practice ran wild, historiographers lost proper reckoning; down to early Han, gnomon observations were uncertain; later mixed observation placed it at twenty-two degrees of Southern Dipper; the Yuanhe calendar used this, matching the ancient calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing submitted: "In the Warring States calendrical practice ran wild, historiographers lost proper reckoning; down to early Han, gnomon observations were uncertain; later mixed observation placed it at Southern Dipper 22°; the Yuanhe calendar used this, matching the ancient calendar.

sentences.zh: 逮至景初，終無毫忒。

translations.literal: Down to the Jingchu era there was never the slightest error."
translations.idiomatic: Down to the Jingchu era there was never the slightest error."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：古術訛雜，其詳闕聞，乙卯之曆，秦代所用，必有效於當時，故其言可征也。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said: Ancient methods were wrong and mixed; details are missing from record; the yimao calendar was used in the Qin era and must have been effective in its time, so its words can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi said: Ancient methods were wrong and mixed; details are missing from record; the yimao calendar was used in the Qin era and must have been effective in its time, so its words can be verified.

sentences.zh: 漢武改創，檢課詳備，正儀審漏，事在前史，測星辨度，理無乖遠。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han reformed and created anew; testing and checking were detailed and complete, correcting instruments and examining clepsydra—the matter is in earlier histories; measuring stars and distinguishing degrees, the principle is not far wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han reformed and created anew; testing and checking were detailed and complete, correcting instruments and examining clepsydra—the matter is in earlier histories; measuring stars and distinguishing degrees, the principle is not far wrong.

sentences.zh: 今議者所是不實見，所非徒為虛妄，辨彼駭此，既非通談，運今背古，所誣誠多，偏據一說，未若兼今之為長也。

translations.literal: What the debaters approve is not real observation; what they reject is merely empty falsity; distinguishing that and rejecting this is not general discussion; applying the present and turning against antiquity, the distortions are indeed many—relying on one theory alone is not as good as combining the present.
translations.idiomatic: What the debaters approve is not real observation; what they reject is merely empty falsity; distinguishing that and rejecting this is not general discussion; applying the present while turning against antiquity, the distortions are indeed many—relying on one theory alone is not as good as combining the present.

sentences.zh: 《景初》之法，實錯五緯，今則在沖口，至曩已移日。

translations.literal: The Jingchu method in fact mis-set the five planets; now it is in Chongzhi's mouth, yet long ago the day had already shifted.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingchu method in fact mis-set the five planets; Dai Faxing now cites it, yet long ago its solar day had already shifted.

sentences.zh: 蓋略治朔望，無事檢候，是以晷漏昏明，並即《元和》，二分異景，尚不知革，日度微差，宜其謬矣。

translations.literal: It roughly handled new and full moons without testing observation; therefore gnomon, clepsydra, dusk and dawn all followed Yuanhe; at the two seasonal nodes the shadows differed, yet they still did not know to reform—solar degree's slight discrepancy ought to have been wrong.
translations.idiomatic: It roughly handled new and full moons without testing observation; therefore gnomon, clepsydra, dusk and dawn all followed Yuanhe; at the two seasonal nodes the shadows differed, yet they still did not know to reform—a slight solar discrepancy was bound to go wrong.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「《書》雲'日短星昴，以正仲冬'。

translations.literal: Faxing submitted: "The Documents say 'The days are short and the stars are the Pleiades—thus the mid-winter is fixed.'
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing submitted: "The Documents say 'The days are short and the Pleiades culminate at dusk—thus mid-winter is fixed.'"

sentences.zh: 直以月推四仲，則中宿常在衛陽，羲、和所以正時，取其萬代不易也。

translations.literal: Taking the moon to push the four mid-season lodges, the central lodges always stand in Weiyang; this is why Xi and He fixed the seasons, taking what would never change for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the moon to push the four seasonal lodges, the central lodges always stand in Weiyang; this is why Xi and He fixed the seasons, taking what would never change for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 沖之以為唐代冬至，日在今宿之左五十許度，遂虛加度分，空撤天路。

translations.literal: Chongzhi holds that in the Tang era the winter solstice stood some fifty degrees to the left of today's lodge, and therefore falsely added degrees and parts, emptying the celestial road."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi holds that at the Tang epoch the winter solstice stood some fifty degrees west of today's position, and on that basis falsely added degrees and parts, emptying the celestial road."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：《書》以上四星昏中審分至者，據人君南面而言也。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said: The Documents, using the four stars' dusk culmination to verify the seasonal nodes, speak from the ruler facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi said: The Documents, using the four stars' dusk culmination to verify the seasonal nodes, speak from the ruler facing south.

sentences.zh: 且南北之正，其詳易准，流見之勢，中天為極。

translations.literal: Moreover the correct north and south are easy to standardize; the trend of setting stars takes mid-heaven as the pole.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover true north and south are easy to standardize; the trend of setting stars takes mid-heaven as the pole.

sentences.zh: 先儒注述，其義僉同，而法興以為《書》說四星，皆在衛陽之位，自在巳地，進失向方，退非始見，迂回經文，以就所執，違訓詭情，此則甚矣。

translations.literal: Former Ru commentaries all agree in meaning, yet Faxing holds that the Documents' four stars all stand in Weiyang, naturally in the si quarter—advancing, he loses direction; retreating, it is not first appearance; twisting the text to fit his hold, violating instruction and distorting meaning—this is extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ru commentaries all agree in meaning, yet Dai Faxing holds that the Documents' four stars all stand in Weiyang, naturally in the si quarter—advancing, he loses direction; retreating, it is not first appearance; twisting the text to fit his hold, violating instruction and distorting meaning—this is extreme.

sentences.zh: 舍午稱巳，午上非無星也。

translations.literal: Abandoning wu and calling it si—above wu there are certainly stars.
translations.idiomatic: Abandoning wu and calling it si—above wu there are certainly stars.

sentences.zh: 必據中宿，餘宿豈複不足以正時。

translations.literal: If one must rely on central lodges, are the other lodges not also sufficient to fix time?
translations.idiomatic: If one must rely on central lodges, are the other lodges not also sufficient to fix time?

sentences.zh: 若謂舉中語兼七列者，觜參尚隱，則不得言，昴星雖見，當雲伏矣，奎婁已見，複不得言伏見囗囗不得以為辭，則名將何附。

translations.literal: If one says mentioning the central stars includes all seven lodges, then Zi and Shen would still be hidden and could not be named; though the Pleiades are visible, one would have to call them hidden; when Kui and Lou are already visible, one again could not speak of hidden or visible [text defective]—this cannot serve as an argument; then to what would the names attach?
translations.idiomatic: If mentioning central stars includes all seven lodges, then Zi and Shen would still be hidden and could not be named; though the Pleiades are visible, one would have to call them hidden; when Kui and Lou are already visible, one again could not speak of hidden or visible [text defective]—this cannot serve as an argument; then to what would the names attach?

sentences.zh: 若中宿之通非允，當實謹檢經旨，直雲星昴，不自衛陽，衛陽無自顯之義，此談何因而立。

translations.literal: If the general rule of central lodges is not allowed, one should strictly examine the classic's intent and simply say "the stars are the Pleiades," not Weiyang; Weiyang has no meaning of self-manifestation—on what basis does this talk stand?
translations.idiomatic: If the general rule of central lodges is not allowed, one should strictly examine the classic's intent and simply say "the stars are the Pleiades," not Weiyang; Weiyang has no meaning of self-manifestation—on what basis does this talk stand?

sentences.zh: 苟理無所依，則可愚辭成說，曾泉、桑野，皆為明證，分至之辨，竟在何日，循複再三，竊深歎息。

translations.literal: If principle has no basis, foolish words can become doctrine; Zeng Spring and Sang Wild are all clear proofs—the distinction of the seasonal nodes, in the end on what day? Going back and forth again and again, I deeply sigh.
translations.idiomatic: If principle has no basis, foolish words can become doctrine; Zeng Spring and Sang Wild are all clear proofs—the distinction of the seasonal nodes, in the end on what day? Going back and forth again and again, I deeply sigh.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「其置法所在，近違半次，則四十五年九月率移一度。

translations.literal: Faxing submitted: "Where his method is set, it nearly violates half a lodge; then every forty-five years and nine months the position shifts one degree."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing submitted: "Where his method is set, it nearly violates half a lodge; then every forty-five years and nine months the position shifts one degree."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：《元和》日度，法興所是，唯征古曆在建星，以今考之，臣法冬至亦在此宿，鬥二十二了無顯證，而虛貶臣曆乖差半次，此愚情之所駭也。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said: The Yuanhe solar degree—Faxing approves it; only citing the ancient calendar in Jianxing—testing by the present, my winter solstice is also in this lodge; Dipper twenty-two has no clear proof, yet he emptily slanders my calendar for half a lodge's error—this is what my humble mind finds shocking.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi said: The Yuanhe solar degree—Dai Faxing approves it; only citing the ancient calendar in Jian—testing by the present, my winter solstice is also in this lodge; Dipper 22 has no clear proof, yet he emptily slanders my calendar for half a lodge's error—this is what my humble mind finds shocking.

sentences.zh: 又年數之餘有十一月，而議雲九月，涉數每乖，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Moreover in the remainder of years there is an eleventh month, yet the objection says the ninth month—when numbers are involved it is often wrong; all are of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover in the remainder of years there is an eleventh month, yet the objection says the ninth month—when numbers are involved it is often wrong; all are of this kind.

sentences.zh: 月盈則食，必在日沖，以檢日則宿度可辨，請據效以課疏密。

translations.literal: When the moon is full it eclipses, necessarily at solar opposition; testing by the day, the lodge degree can be distinguished—please test by results to examine coarse and fine.
translations.idiomatic: When the moon is full it eclipses, necessarily at solar opposition; testing by the day, the lodge degree can be distinguished—please test by results to examine coarse and fine.

sentences.zh: 按太史注記，元嘉十三年十二月十六日中夜月蝕盡，在鬼四度，以沖計之，日當在牛六。

translations.literal: Examining the Grand Clerk's annotated record: in Yuanjia year 13, month 12, day 16, at midnight the moon was fully eclipsed at Ghost 4 degrees; by my calculation the sun ought to have been at Ox 6.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Grand Clerk's annotated record: in Yuanjia year 13, month 12, day 16, at midnight the moon was fully eclipsed at Ghost 4°; by my calculation the sun ought to have been at Ox 6.

sentences.zh: 依法興議：「在女七」。

translations.literal: By Faxing's objection: "at Woman 7."
translations.idiomatic: By Dai Faxing's objection: "at Woman 7."

sentences.zh: 又十四年五月十五日丁夜月蝕盡，在鬥二十六度，以沖計之，日當在井三十，依法興議曰：「日在柳二。

translations.literal: Again in year 14, month 5, day 15, at the ding night the moon was fully eclipsed at Dipper 26 degrees; by my calculation the sun ought to have been at Well 30; by Faxing's objection: "the sun at Willow 2."
translations.idiomatic: Again in year 14, month 5, day 15, at the ding night the moon was fully eclipsed at Dipper 26°; by my calculation the sun ought to have been at Well 30; by Dai Faxing's objection: "the sun at Willow 2."

sentences.zh: 」又二十八年八月十五日丁夜月蝕，在奎十一度，以沖計之，日當在角二；

translations.literal: Again in year 28, month 8, day 15, at the ding night there was a lunar eclipse at Kui 11 degrees; by my calculation the sun ought to have been at Horn 2;
translations.idiomatic: Again in year 28, month 8, day 15, at the ding night there was a lunar eclipse at Kui 11°; by my calculation the sun ought to have been at Horn 2;

sentences.zh: 依法興議曰：「日在角十二。

translations.literal: By Faxing's objection: "the sun at Horn 12."
translations.idiomatic: By Dai Faxing's objection: "the sun at Horn 12."

sentences.zh: 」又大明三年九月十五日乙夜月蝕盡，在胃宿之末，以沖計之，日當在氐十二；

translations.literal: Again in Daming year 3, month 9, day 15, at the yi night the moon was fully eclipsed at the end of Stomach lodge; by my calculation the sun ought to have been at Base 12;
translations.idiomatic: Again in Daming year 3, month 9, day 15, at the yi night the moon was fully eclipsed at the end of Stomach lodge; by my calculation the sun ought to have been at Base 12;

sentences.zh: 依法興議曰：「日在心二。

translations.literal: By Faxing's objection: "the sun at Heart 2."
translations.idiomatic: By Dai Faxing's objection: "the sun at Heart 2."

sentences.zh: 」凡此四蝕，皆與臣法符同，纖毫不爽，而法興所據，頓差十度，違沖移宿，顯然易睹。

translations.literal: All four eclipses match my method exactly, not the slightest discrepancy, while Faxing's basis suddenly differs by ten degrees, violating Chongzhi's shifted lodge—clear and easy to see.
translations.idiomatic: All four eclipses match my method exactly, not the slightest discrepancy, while Dai Faxing's basis suddenly differs by ten degrees, violating the shifted lodge—clear and easy to see.

sentences.zh: 故知天數漸差，則當式遵以為典，事驗昭晰，豈得信古而疑今。

translations.literal: Therefore one knows celestial numbers gradually shift; one ought then to follow them as standard; the test is clear and bright—how can one trust antiquity and doubt the present?
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one knows celestial numbers gradually shift; one ought then to follow them as standard; the test is clear and bright—how can one trust antiquity and doubt the present?

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「在《詩》'七月流火'，此夏正建申之時也。

translations.literal: Faxing submitted: "In the Odes, 'In the seventh month the Fire Star sets,' marks the time when the Xia calendar takes shen as first month.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing submitted: "In the Odes, 'In the seventh month the Fire Star sets,' marks the time when the Xia calendar takes shen as first month.

sentences.zh: '定之方中'，又小雪之節也。

translations.literal: 'Ding is centered in the square' is again the Lesser Snow node.
translations.idiomatic: 'Ding stands centered in the square' is again the Lesser Snow node.

sentences.zh: 若冬至審差，則豳公火流，晷長一尺五寸，楚宮之作，晝漏五十三刻，此詭之甚也。

translations.literal: If the winter solstice were truly displaced, then in Duke of Bin's time the Fire Star would set, the gnomon shadow would be one chi five cun long, and when the Chu palace was built the day clepsydra would run fifty-three marks—an extreme absurdity."
translations.idiomatic: If the solstice were truly off by his amount, the Fire Star would set in Duke Bin's day, noon shadows would measure one chi five cun, and the Chu palace would have been built with a fifty-three-mark day clepsydra—an extreme absurdity."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：臣按此議三條皆謬。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said: I hold that on all three points of this objection he is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi said: I hold that on all three points of this objection he is wrong.

sentences.zh: 《詩》稱流火，蓋略舉西移之中，以為驚寒之候。

translations.literal: The Odes speak of the setting Fire Star, broadly taking the middle of westward movement as the sign of approaching cold.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes speak of the setting Fire Star, broadly taking the middle of westward movement as the sign of approaching cold.

sentences.zh: 流之為言，非始動之辭也。

translations.literal: Setting as a word is not the language of first motion.
translations.idiomatic: "Setting" as a word is not the language of first motion.

sentences.zh: 就如始說，冬至日度在鬥二十二，則火星之中，當在大暑之前，豈鄰建申之限。

translations.literal: Just as in his first claim, if the winter solstice's solar degree were at Dipper twenty-two, then the Fire Star's central passage would fall before Great Heat—how could it border the limit of jian-shen?
translations.idiomatic: Just as in his first claim, if the solstice's solar degree were at Dipper 22, then the Fire Star's central passage would fall before Great Heat—how could it border the limit of jian-shen?

sentences.zh: 此專自攻糾，非謂矯失。

translations.literal: This is solely self-contradictory attack—not saying he falsifies error.
translations.idiomatic: This is solely self-contradictory attack—not saying he falsifies error.

sentences.zh: 《夏小正》：「五月昏，大火中。

translations.literal: The Xia Small Calendar: "In the fifth month at dusk, the Great Fire is central."
translations.idiomatic: The Xia Small Calendar: "In the fifth month at dusk, the Great Fire is central."

sentences.zh: 」此複在衛陽之地乎？

translations.literal: Is this again in Weiyang's place?
translations.idiomatic: Is this again in Weiyang's place?

sentences.zh: 又謂臣所立法，楚宮之作，在九月初。

translations.literal: He also says the method I established places the Chu palace's building in early ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: He also says the method I established places the Chu palace's building in early ninth month.

sentences.zh: 按《詩》傳箋皆謂定之方中者，室辟昏中，形四方也。

translations.literal: Examining Odes commentary and notes, all say "Ding is centered in the square" means Room's wall is centrally dark, forming a square.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Odes commentary and notes, all say "Ding stands centered in the square" means Room's wall is centrally dark, forming a square.

sentences.zh: 然則中天之正，當在室之八度。

translations.literal: Then mid-heaven's correct point ought to be at Room's eighth degree.
translations.idiomatic: Then mid-heaven's correct point ought to be at Room 8°.

sentences.zh: 臣曆推之，元年立冬後四日，此度昏中，乃處十月之初，又非寒露之日也。

translations.literal: My calendar pushes it: four days after Beginning of Winter in year 1, this degree is centrally dark, and it falls at the start of the tenth month—not again the Cold Dew day.
translations.idiomatic: My calendar pushes it: four days after Beginning of Winter in year 1, this degree is centrally dark, and it falls at the start of the tenth month—not again the Cold Dew day.

sentences.zh: 議者之意，蓋誤以周世為堯時，度差五十，故致此謬。

translations.literal: The objector's intent probably mistakes the Zhou age for Yao's time; the degree difference of fifty therefore causes this error.
translations.idiomatic: The objector's intent probably mistakes the Zhou age for Yao's time; the fifty-degree difference therefore causes this error.

sentences.zh: 小雪之節，自信之談，非有明文可據也。

translations.literal: The Lesser Snow node is self-confident talk, with no clear text for proof.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Snow node is self-confident talk, with no clear text for proof.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「仲尼曰：'丘聞之，火伏而後蟄者畢。

translations.literal: Faxing submitted: "Confucius said: 'I have heard that after the Fire Star sets, all hibernating creatures are finished.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing submitted: "Confucius said: 'I have heard that after the Fire Star sets, every hibernating creature has finished its dormancy.

sentences.zh: 今火猶西流，司曆過也。

translations.literal: Now the Fire Star still moves westward—the calendar officer has gone too far.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Confucius' day the Fire Star was still moving westward—the calendar officer had fallen behind.'"

sentences.zh: '就如沖之所誤，則星無定次，卦有差方，名號之正，古今必殊，典誥之音，時不通軌。

translations.literal: If it were as Chongzhi errs, then stars would have no fixed order and the hexagrams would have displaced directions; correct names of old and present must differ; the sounds of canonical edicts cannot match across ages.
translations.idiomatic: If it were as Zu Chongzhi errs, then stars would have no fixed order and the hexagrams would have displaced directions; correct names of old and present must differ; the sounds of canonical edicts cannot match across ages.

sentences.zh: 堯之開、閉，今成建、除，今之壽星，乃周之鶉尾也。

translations.literal: Yao's Opening and Closing become today's Establishment and Removal; today's Longevity Star was Zhou's Chimei Tail.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's Opening and Closing become today's Establishment and Removal; today's Longevity Star was Zhou's Chimei Tail.

sentences.zh: 即時東壁，已非玄武，軫星頓屬蒼龍，誣天背經，乃至於此。

translations.literal: At present Eastern Wall is no longer Dark Warrior, and Chariot stars suddenly belong to Azure Dragon—distorting Heaven and violating the classics, even to this extent."
translations.idiomatic: At present Eastern Wall is no longer Dark Warrior, and Chariot suddenly belongs to Azure Dragon—distorting Heaven and violating the classics to this degree."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：臣以為辰極居中，而列曜貞觀，群像殊體，而陰陽區別，故羽介咸陳，則水火有位，蒼素齊設，則東西可准，非以日之所在，定其名號也。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said: I hold that the pole star stands at center while the arrayed luminaries keep fixed observation; the images differ in form while yin and yang are distinguished; therefore feathered and shelled are all arrayed, then water and fire have their places; azure and white are equally set, then east and west can be standardized—not by where the sun stands to fix names.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi said: I hold that the pole star stands at center while the arrayed luminaries keep fixed observation; the images differ in form while yin and yang are distinguished; therefore feathered and shelled are all arrayed, then water and fire have their places; azure and white are equally set, then east and west can be standardized—not by where the sun stands to fix names.

sentences.zh: 何以明之？

translations.literal: How is this clear?
translations.idiomatic: How is this clear?

sentences.zh: 夫陽爻初九，氣始正北，玄武七列，虛當子位。

translations.literal: At the first nine of the yang line, qi first stands due north; the seven ranks of Dark Warrior, Void occupies the zi position.
translations.idiomatic: At the first nine of the yang line, qi first stands due north; the seven ranks of Dark Warrior, Void occupies the zi position.

sentences.zh: 若圓儀辨方，以日為主，冬至所舍，當在玄枵；

translations.literal: If the circular instrument distinguishes direction with the sun as master, where the winter solstice lodges ought to be in Dark Establishment;
translations.idiomatic: If the circular instrument distinguishes direction with the sun as master, where the winter solstice lodges ought to be in Dark Establishment;

sentences.zh: 而今之南極，乃處東維，違體失中，其義何附。

translations.literal: yet today's south pole is in the eastern cord—violating form and losing center; to what principle does this attach?
translations.idiomatic: yet today's south pole is in the eastern cord—violating form and losing center; to what principle does this attach?

sentences.zh: 若南北以冬夏稟稱，則卯酉以生殺定號，豈得春躔義方，秋麗仁域，名舛理乖，若此之反哉！

translations.literal: If north and south are named by winter and summer's endowment, then mao and you ought to be fixed by birth and killing—how could spring lodge in the domain of righteousness and autumn stand in the domain of benevolence—names wrong and principle twisted, so contrary!
translations.idiomatic: If north and south are named by winter and summer's endowment, then mao and you ought to be fixed by birth and killing—how could spring lodge in the domain of righteousness and autumn stand in the domain of benevolence—names wrong and principle twisted, so contrary!

sentences.zh: 因茲以言，因知天以列宿分方，而不在於四時，景緯環序，日不獨守故轍矣。

translations.literal: From this one speaks, and knows Heaven divides direction by arrayed lodges, not by the four seasons; the bright cords circle in order, and the sun does not alone keep its old track.
translations.idiomatic: From this one speaks, and knows Heaven divides direction by arrayed lodges, not by the four seasons; the bright cords circle in order, and the sun does not alone keep its old track.

sentences.zh: 至於中星見伏，記籍每以審時者，蓋以歷數難詳，而天驗易顯，各據一代所合，以為簡易之政也。

translations.literal: As for central stars' visibility and hiding, records often use them to verify seasons because calendrical numbers are hard to detail while celestial tests are easy to show—each relies on what matched one age as a simple policy.
translations.idiomatic: As for central stars' visibility and hiding, records often use them to verify seasons because calendrical numbers are hard to detail while celestial tests are easy to show—each relies on what matched one age as a simple policy.

sentences.zh: 亦猶夏禮未通商典，《濩》容豈襲《韶》節，誠天人之道同差，則藝之興，因代而推移矣。

translations.literal: It is also like Xia rites not matching Shang canons—how could Hu's music inherit Shao's measure; truly if Heaven and man's ways differ alike, then the rise of arts shifts with the age.
translations.idiomatic: It is also like Xia rites not matching Shang canons—how could Hu's music inherit Shao's measure; truly if Heaven and man's ways differ alike, then the rise of arts shifts with the age.

sentences.zh: 月位稱建，諒以氣之所本，名隨實著，非謂鬥杓所指。

translations.literal: Calling the month's position Establishment plainly takes the qi's root; the name follows the reality—it does not mean the Dipper handle's pointing.
translations.idiomatic: Calling the month's position Establishment plainly takes the qi's root; the name follows the reality—it does not mean the Dipper handle's pointing.

sentences.zh: 近校漢時，已差半次，審鬥節時，其效安在。

translations.literal: Testing near Han times, it already differed by half a lodge; verifying Dipper-node seasons, where is the effect?
translations.idiomatic: Testing near Han times, it already differed by half a lodge; verifying Dipper-node seasons, where is the effect?

sentences.zh: 或義非經訓，依以成說，將緯候多詭，偽辭間設乎？

translations.literal: Or if meaning is not from classic instruction, relying on it to make doctrine—will apocryphal observations be mostly strange and false words occasionally set?
translations.idiomatic: Or if meaning is not from classic instruction, relying on it to make doctrine—will apocryphal observations be mostly strange and false words occasionally set?

sentences.zh: 次隨方名，義合宿體。

translations.literal: Next, following direction names, meaning matches lodge form.
translations.idiomatic: Next, following direction names, meaning matches lodge form.

sentences.zh: 分至雖遷，而厥位不改，豈謂龍火貿處，金水亂列，名號乖殊之譏，抑未詳究。

translations.literal: Though the seasonal nodes shift, their positions do not change—does one mean Dragon and Fire trade places, Metal and Water disorder the array—the reproach of mismatched names? I have not yet examined it in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Though the seasonal nodes shift, their positions do not change—does one mean Dragon and Fire trade places, Metal and Water disorder the array—the reproach of mismatched names? I have not yet examined it in detail.

sentences.zh: 至如壁非玄武，軫屬蒼龍，瞻度察晷，實效鹹然。

translations.literal: As for Wall not being Dark Warrior and Chariot belonging to Azure Dragon—observing degrees and examining gnomon, the real effect is indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: As for Wall not being Dark Warrior and Chariot belonging to Azure Dragon—observing degrees and examining gnomon, the real effect is indeed so.

sentences.zh: 《元嘉曆法》，壽星之初，亦在翼限，參校晉注，顯驗甚眾。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia calendar method, at the start of the Longevity Star it was also in Wings' limit; comparing Jin commentary, clear proofs are many.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia calendar method, at the start of the Longevity Star it was also in Wings' limit; comparing Jin commentary, clear proofs are many.

sentences.zh: 天數差移，百有餘載，議者誠能馳辭騁辯，令南極非冬至，望不在沖，則此談乃可守耳。

translations.literal: Celestial numbers shift over more than a hundred years; if the debater can truly gallop words and race argument, making the south pole not the winter solstice and full moon not at opposition—then this talk could be kept.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial numbers shift over more than a hundred years; if the debater can truly gallop words and race argument, making the south pole not the winter solstice and full moon not at opposition—then this talk could be kept.

sentences.zh: 若使日遷次留，則無事屢嫌，乃臣曆之良證，非難者所宜列也。

translations.literal: If the sun keeps shifting lodge and pausing, then there is no need for repeated suspicion—this is good proof of my calendar, not what objectors ought to list.
translations.idiomatic: If the sun keeps shifting lodge and pausing, then there is no need for repeated suspicion—this is good proof of my calendar, not what objectors ought to list.

sentences.zh: 尋臣所執，必據經史，遠考唐典，近征漢籍，讖記碎言，不敢依述，竊謂循經之論也。

translations.literal: Examining what I hold, I must rely on classics and history, examining Tang canons in the distance and Han records near at hand; apocryphal fragments I dare not follow—I deem this discussion that follows the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Examining what I hold, I must rely on classics and history, examining Tang canons in the distance and Han records near at hand; apocryphal fragments I dare not follow—I deem this discussion that follows the classics.

sentences.zh: 月蝕檢日度，事驗昭著，史注詳論，文存禁閣，斯又稽天之說也。

translations.literal: Testing solar degree by lunar eclipse, the proof is clear and bright; history's annotated discussion survives in the forbidden archive—this again is investigation of Heaven's sayings.
translations.idiomatic: Testing solar degree by lunar eclipse, the proof is clear and bright; history's annotated discussion survives in the forbidden archive—this again is investigation of Heaven's sayings.

sentences.zh: 《堯典》四星，並在衛陽，今之日度，遠淮元和，誣背之誚，實此之謂。

translations.literal: The Canons of Yao's four stars all stand in Weiyang; today's solar degree is far from Yuanhe—the reproach of distortion and violation is exactly this.
translations.idiomatic: The Canons of Yao's four stars all stand in Weiyang; today's solar degree is far from Yuanhe—the reproach of distortion and violation is exactly this.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「夫日有緩急，故鬥有闊狹，古人制章，立為中格，年積十九，常有七閏，晷或盈虛，此不可革。

translations.literal: Faxing submitted: "The sun has slow and fast motion, therefore the Dipper has wide and narrow openings; the ancients set the rule at a middle standard; over nineteen accumulated years there are always seven intercalations; the gnomon may be empty or full—this cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing submitted: "Because the sun's motion varies, the Dipper's opening varies in width; the ancients fixed the rule at a middle standard—over nineteen years there are always seven intercalations, and gnomon readings may run slightly long or short—this cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 沖之削閏壞章，倍減餘數，則一百三十九年二月，於四分之科，頓少一日；

translations.literal: Chongzhi cuts intercalations and breaks the rule, halving the remainder numbers; then in one hundred thirty-nine years and two months, under the Quarter-Remainder standard, one day is suddenly lost;
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi cuts intercalations and breaks the rule, halving the remainder numbers; then in 139 years and two months, on the Quarter-Remainder standard, one day is suddenly lost;

sentences.zh: 七千四百二十九年，輒失一閏。

translations.literal: in seven thousand four hundred twenty-nine years one intercalation is lost.
translations.idiomatic: in 7,429 years one intercalation is lost.

sentences.zh: 夫日少則先時，閏失則事悖。

translations.literal: If days are too few, the seasons come early; if intercalations are lost, affairs go wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Too few days make the seasons run early; lost intercalations make affairs fall out of step.

sentences.zh: 竊聞時以作事，事以厚生，此乃生民之所本，歷數之所先。

translations.literal: I have heard that seasons govern work, and work nourishes life—this is the foundation of the people and the first of calendrical numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Seasons govern work, and work sustains life—this is the foundation of the people and the first of calendrical numbers.

sentences.zh: 愚恐非沖之淺慮，妄可穿鑿。

translations.literal: I fear this is not something Chongzhi's shallow thinking can arbitrarily rework."
translations.idiomatic: I fear this is not something Zu Chongzhi's shallow thinking can arbitrarily rework."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：按《後漢書》及《乾象說》，《四分曆法》，雖分章設篰創自元和，而晷儀眾數定于嘉平三年。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said: Examining the Book of Later Han and the Qianxiang Treatise, the Quarter-Remainder calendar method, though dividing the rule and setting bamboo markers was created from Yuanhe, gnomon instruments and many numbers were fixed in Jiaoping year 3.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi said: Examining the Book of Later Han and the Qianxiang Treatise, the Quarter-Remainder calendar method, though dividing the rule and setting bamboo markers was created from Yuanhe, gnomon instruments and many numbers were fixed in Jiaoping year 3.

sentences.zh: 《四分志》，立冬中影長一丈，立春中影九尺六寸。

translations.literal: The Quarter-Remainder Treatise: at Beginning of Winter the central shadow is one zhang long; at Beginning of Spring the central shadow is nine chi six cun.
translations.idiomatic: The Quarter-Remainder Treatise: at Beginning of Winter the central shadow is one zhang long; at Beginning of Spring the central shadow is nine chi six cun.

sentences.zh: 尋冬至南極，日晷最長，二氣去至，日數既同，則中影應等，而前長後短，頓差四寸，此曆景冬至後天之驗也。

translations.literal: Examining the winter solstice south pole, the sun's gnomon is longest; the two qi depart from the solstice with equal day-count, so the central shadow ought to be equal—yet the former is long and the latter short, suddenly differing four cun—this is the calendar shadow's proof that the winter solstice lags Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the winter solstice south pole, the sun's gnomon is longest; the two qi depart from the solstice with equal day-count, so the central shadow ought to be equal—yet the former is long and the latter short, suddenly differing four cun—this is the calendar shadow's proof that the winter solstice lags Heaven.

sentences.zh: 二氣中影，日差九分半弱，進退均調，略無盈縮。

translations.literal: The two qi's central shadows differ by nine fen and a half weak in day-count; advance and retreat are evenly adjusted, roughly without surplus or shrinkage.
translations.idiomatic: The two qi's central shadows differ by nine fen and a half weak in day-count; advance and retreat are evenly adjusted, roughly without surplus or shrinkage.

sentences.zh: 以率計之，二氣各退二日十二刻，則晷影之數，立冬更短，立春更長，並差二寸，二氣中影俱長九尺八寸矣。

translations.literal: Calculating by rate, each qi retreats two days twelve marks; then the gnomon shadow numbers—Beginning of Winter shorter, Beginning of Spring longer—both differ two cun; the two qi's central shadows are both nine chi eight cun long.
translations.idiomatic: Calculating by rate, each qi retreats two days twelve marks; then the gnomon shadow numbers—Beginning of Winter shorter, Beginning of Spring longer—both differ two cun; the two qi's central shadows are both nine chi eight cun long.

sentences.zh: 即立冬、立春之正日也。

translations.literal: That is the correct day of Beginning of Winter and Beginning of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: That is the correct day of Beginning of Winter and Beginning of Spring.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，曆置冬至，後天亦二日十二刻也。

translations.literal: Pushing from this, the calendar's set winter solstice also lags Heaven by two days twelve marks.
translations.idiomatic: Pushing from this, the calendar's set winter solstice also lags Heaven by two days twelve marks.

sentences.zh: 嘉平三年，時曆丁醜冬至，加時正在日中。

translations.literal: In Jiaoping year 3, the calendar's dingchou winter solstice, the added hour was exactly at midday.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaoping year 3, the calendar's dingchou winter solstice, the added hour was exactly at midday.

sentences.zh: 以二日十二刻減之，天定以乙亥冬至，加時在夜半後三十八刻。

translations.literal: Subtracting two days twelve marks, Heaven fixes yihai winter solstice, the added hour at thirty-eight marks after midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting two days twelve marks, Heaven fixes yihai winter solstice, the added hour at thirty-eight marks after midnight.

sentences.zh: 又臣測景曆紀，躬辨分寸，銅表堅剛，暴潤不動，光晷明潔，纖毫盡然。

translations.literal: Moreover I measured shadows over calendar eras, personally distinguishing fen and cun; the bronze table was firm and rigid, swelling and wetting did not move it; the light gnomon was bright and clean, the slightest hair was clear.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I measured shadows over calendar eras, personally distinguishing fen and cun; the bronze table was firm and rigid, swelling and wetting did not move it; the light gnomon was bright and clean, the slightest hair was clear.

sentences.zh: 據大明五年十月十日，影一丈七寸七分半，十一月二十五日，一丈八寸一分太，二十六日，一丈七寸五分強，折取其中，則中天冬至，應在十一月三日。

translations.literal: According to Daming year 5, month 10, day 10, shadow one chi seven cun seven fen half; month 11, day 25, one chi eight cun one fen tai; day 26, one chi seven cun five fen strong; taking the mean, mid-heaven winter solstice ought to fall on month 11, day 3.
translations.idiomatic: According to Daming year 5, month 10, day 10, shadow one chi seven cun seven fen half; month 11, day 25, one chi eight cun one fen tai; day 26, one chi seven cun five fen strong; taking the mean, mid-heaven winter solstice ought to fall on month 11, day 3.

sentences.zh: 求其蚤晚，令後二日影相減，則一日差率也。

translations.literal: Seeking early and late, let the shadows of the next two days be subtracted—then the one-day difference rate.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking early and late, let the shadows of the next two days be subtracted—then the one-day difference rate.

sentences.zh: 倍之為法，前二日減，以百刻乘之為實，以法除實，得冬至加時在夜半後三十一刻，在《元嘉曆》後一日，天數之正也。

translations.literal: Doubling it makes the divisor; subtract the previous two days, multiply by one hundred marks for the dividend, divide the dividend by the divisor—the winter solstice added hour is thirty-one marks after midnight, one day after the Yuanjia calendar—the correction of celestial numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Doubling it makes the divisor; subtract the previous two days, multiply by one hundred marks for the dividend, divide the dividend by the divisor—the winter solstice added hour is thirty-one marks after midnight, one day after the Yuanjia calendar—the correction of celestial numbers.

sentences.zh: 量檢竟年，則數減均同，異歲相課，則遠近應率。

translations.literal: Measuring and checking the whole year, the numbers decrease equally; testing different years, near and far match the rate.
translations.idiomatic: Measuring and checking the whole year, the numbers decrease equally; testing different years, near and far match the rate.

sentences.zh: 臣因此驗，考正章法。

translations.literal: From this test I corrected the rule.
translations.idiomatic: From this test I corrected the rule.

sentences.zh: 今以臣曆推之，刻如前，竊謂至密，永為定式。

translations.literal: Now pushing by my calendar, the marks as before—I deem it extremely precise and forever the fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Now pushing by my calendar, the marks as before—I deem it extremely precise and forever the fixed pattern.

sentences.zh: 尋古曆法並同《四分》，《四分》之數久則後天，經三百年，朔差一日。

translations.literal: Examining ancient calendar methods, all match the Quarter-Remainder; the Quarter-Remainder numbers over long time lag Heaven; over three hundred years new moons miss one day.
translations.idiomatic: Examining ancient calendar methods, all match the Quarter-Remainder; the Quarter-Remainder numbers over long time lag Heaven; over three hundred years new moons miss one day.

sentences.zh: 是以漢載四百，食率在晦。

translations.literal: Therefore in Han's four hundred years, eclipses often fell on last days.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in Han's four hundred years, eclipses often fell on last days.

sentences.zh: 魏代已來，遂革斯法，世莫之非者，誠有效於天也。

translations.literal: From Wei onward they reformed this method; the world none faulted it—truly it was effective with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei onward they reformed this method; no one faulted it—truly it was effective with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 章歲十九，其疏尤甚，同出前術，非見經典。

translations.literal: Rule years nineteen—its coarseness is especially great; it comes from earlier methods alike, not seen in classics.
translations.idiomatic: Rule years nineteen—its coarseness is especially great; it comes from earlier methods alike, not seen in classics.

sentences.zh: 而議雲此法自古，數不可移。

translations.literal: Yet the objection says this method is ancient and the number cannot be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the objection says this method is ancient and the number cannot be moved.

sentences.zh: 若古法雖疏，永當循用，謬論誠立，則法興複欲施《四分》於當今矣，理容然乎？

translations.literal: If ancient methods though coarse must forever be followed, the false argument is truly established—then Faxing again wants to apply the Quarter-Remainder to the present day; is that reasonable?
translations.idiomatic: If ancient methods though coarse must forever be followed, the false argument is truly established—then Dai Faxing again wants to apply the Quarter-Remainder to the present day; is that reasonable?

sentences.zh: 臣所未譬也。

translations.literal: This is what I have not understood.
translations.idiomatic: This is what I have not understood.

sentences.zh: 若謂今所革創違舛失衷者，未聞顯據有以矯奪臣法也。

translations.literal: If one says what I now reform violates error and misses the mean, I have not heard clear proof sufficient to overturn my method.
translations.idiomatic: If one says what I now reform violates error and misses the mean, I have not heard clear proof sufficient to overturn my method.

sentences.zh: 《元嘉曆》術，減閏餘二，直以襲舊分粗，故進退未合。

translations.literal: The Yuanjia calendar method reduced intercalation remainder by two, directly inheriting the old coarse fraction, so advance and retreat did not match.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanjia calendar method reduced intercalation remainder by two, directly inheriting the old coarse fraction, so advance and retreat did not match.

sentences.zh: 至於棄盈求正，非為乖理。

translations.literal: As for abandoning surplus to seek correctness, it is not violating principle.
translations.idiomatic: As for abandoning surplus to seek correctness, it is not violating principle.

sentences.zh: 就如議意，率不可易，則分無增損，承天置法，複為違謬。

translations.literal: Just as in the objection's intent, if the rate cannot be changed, then the fraction has no increase or decrease—setting the method to match Heaven again becomes wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Just as in the objection's intent, if the rate cannot be changed, then the fraction has no increase or decrease—setting the method to match Heaven again becomes wrong.

sentences.zh: 節氣蚤晚，當循《景初》，二至差三日，曾不覺其非，橫謂臣曆為失，知日少之先時，未悟增月甚惑也。

translations.literal: Whether solar nodes come early or late ought to follow Jingchu; the two solstices differ by three days, yet he never notices the error, and groundlessly says my calendar is wrong—knowing days are too few makes seasons early, yet not understanding the added month is very confused.
translations.idiomatic: Whether solar nodes come early or late ought to follow Jingchu; the two solstices differ by three days, yet he never notices the error, and groundlessly says my calendar is wrong—knowing days are too few makes seasons early, yet not understanding the added month is very confused.

sentences.zh: 誠未睹天驗，豈測歷數之要，生民之本，諒非率意所斷矣。

translations.literal: Truly not seeing celestial tests, how can one measure the essentials of calendrical numbers—the foundation of the people is surely not what arbitrary intent can decide.
translations.idiomatic: Truly not seeing celestial tests, how can one measure the essentials of calendrical numbers—the foundation of the people is surely not what arbitrary intent can decide.

sentences.zh: 又法興始雲窮識晷變，可以刊舊革今，複謂晷數盈虛，不可為准，互自違伐，罔識所依。

translations.literal: Moreover Faxing first said that fully knowing gnomon change could edit the old and reform the present, yet again says gnomon numbers empty and full cannot be standard—mutually contradicting himself, not knowing what he relies on.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Dai Faxing first said that fully knowing gnomon change could edit the old and reform the present, yet again says gnomon numbers empty and full cannot be standard—mutually contradicting himself, not knowing what he relies on.

sentences.zh: 若推步不得准，天功絕於心目，未詳曆紀何 因而立。

translations.literal: If computation cannot be standard, Heaven's work is cut off from eye and mind—I do not know on what basis the calendar was established.
translations.idiomatic: If computation cannot be standard, Heaven's work is cut off from eye and mind—I do not know on what basis the calendar was established.

sentences.zh: 案《春秋》以來千有餘載，以食檢朔，曾無差失，此則日行有恆之明征也。

translations.literal: Examining from the Spring and Autumn Annals for more than a thousand years, testing new moons by eclipses, there was never error—this is clear proof that the sun's motion is constant.
translations.idiomatic: Examining from the Spring and Autumn Annals for more than a thousand years, testing new moons by eclipses, there was never error—this is clear proof that the sun's motion is constant.

sentences.zh: 且臣考影彌年，窮察毫微，課驗以前，合若符契，孟子以為千歲之日至，可坐而知，斯言實矣。

translations.literal: Moreover I tested shadows over many years, examining to the slightest hair; testing against earlier methods, the match is like seal and tally; Mencius held that a thousand years' solstice could be known sitting—this saying is true.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I tested shadows over many years, examining to the slightest hair; testing against earlier methods, the match is like seal and tally; Mencius held that a thousand years' solstice could be known sitting—this saying is true.

sentences.zh: 日有緩急，未見其證，浮辭虛貶，竊非所懼。

translations.literal: The sun's slow and fast motion—I have not seen its proof; floating words and empty slander I am not afraid of.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's slow and fast motion—I have not seen its proof; floating words and empty slander I am not afraid of.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「沖之既雲冬至歲差，又謂虛為北中，舍形責影，未足為迷。

translations.literal: Faxing submitted: "Chongzhi both claims winter-solstice precession and says Void is northern center; abandoning form and blaming the shadow is not enough to count as error.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing submitted: "Zu Chongzhi both claims solstice precession and calls Void the northern center; abandoning form for shadow alone is not yet proof of error.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 凡在天非日不明，居地以鬥而辨，借令冬至在虛，則黃道彌遠，東北當為黃鐘之宮，室壁應屬玄枵之位，虛宿豈得複為北中乎？

translations.literal: In Heaven nothing is clear without the sun; on earth one distinguishes by the Dipper; suppose the winter solstice were in Void, then the Yellow Path would be farther away; northeast ought to be the palace of Yellow Bell, and Room-Wall ought to belong to Dark Establishment—how could Void again be northern center?
translations.idiomatic: In the sky nothing is clear without the sun; on earth one orients by the Dipper; suppose the solstice stood in Void, the ecliptic would lie farther out, northeast ought to be Yellow Bell's palace, and Room-Wall ought to fall in Dark Establishment—how could Void still be the northern center?

sentences.zh: 曲使分至屢遷，而星次不改，招搖易繩，而律呂仍往，則七政不以璣衡致齊，建時亦非攝提所紀，不知五行何居，六屬安托。

translations.literal: Forcing the four seasonal nodes to shift repeatedly while star orders do not change, changing the Dipper's cord while pitch-pipes stay as before—then the seven regulators would not be aligned by the armillary, and Establishment time would not be marked by Sagittarius; one would not know where the Five Phases dwell or where the six domains rest."
translations.idiomatic: Forcing the seasonal nodes to keep shifting while lodge order stays fixed, moving the Dipper cord while pitch-pipes remain unchanged—the seven regulators would not align by the armillary, Establishment time would not be marked by Sagittarius, and one would not know where the Five Phases or six domains belong."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：此條所嫌，前牒已詳。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said: The objection on this item was already detailed in the earlier memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi said: The objection on this item was already detailed in the earlier memorial.

sentences.zh: 次改方移，虛非中位，繁辭廣證，自構紛惑，皆議者所謬誤，非臣法之違設也。

translations.literal: Next, changing lodge position—Void is not the central position; verbose words and broad proofs self-construct confusion—all are the debater's errors, not violations of my method's setting.
translations.idiomatic: Next, changing lodge position—Void is not the central position; verbose words and broad proofs self-construct confusion—all are the debater's errors, not violations of my method's setting.

sentences.zh: 七政致齊，實謂天儀，鄭、王唱述，厥訓明允，雖有異說，蓋非實義。

translations.literal: The seven regulators' alignment truly means the celestial instrument; Zheng and Wang proclaimed and set forth—their instruction is clear and fair; though there are differing sayings, they are mostly not real meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The seven regulators' alignment truly means the celestial instrument; Zheng and Wang proclaimed and set forth—their instruction is clear and fair; though there are differing sayings, they are mostly not real meaning.

sentences.zh: 法興議曰：「夫置元設紀，各有所尚，或據文於圖讖，或取效於當時。

translations.literal: Faxing submitted: "Setting the origin and establishing the era each follow different preferences—some rely on apocryphal texts, some take proof from their own time.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing submitted: "Setting the origin and establishing the era each follow different preferences—some rely on apocryphal texts, some take proof from their own time.

sentences.zh: 沖之雲'群氏糾紛，莫審其會。

translations.literal: Chongzhi says 'Schools dispute endlessly and none can verify the conjunction.'
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi says 'Schools dispute endlessly and none can verify the conjunction.'"

sentences.zh: '昔《黃帝》辛卯，日月不過，《顓頊》乙卯，四時不忒，《景初》壬辰，晦無差光，《元嘉》庚辰，朔無錯景，豈非承天者乎？

translations.literal: Formerly the Yellow Emperor calendar used xinmao, sun and moon never exceeded; Zhuanxu used yimao, the four seasons were never off; Jingchu used renchen, last days of months had no light error; Yuanjia used gengchen, new moons had no shadow error—were these not calendars that matched Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor calendar used xinmao, sun and moon never exceeded; Zhuanxu used yimao, the four seasons were never off; Jingchu used renchen, last-day moons had no light error; Yuanjia used gengchen, new moons had no shadow error—were these not Heaven-conforming calendars?

sentences.zh: 沖之苟存甲子，可謂為合以求天也。

translations.literal: If Chongzhi arbitrarily keeps jiazi, one may say he matched to seek Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: If Zu Chongzhi arbitrarily keeps jiazi, one may say he forced a fit to seek Heaven's approval."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：夫曆存效密，不容殊尚，合讖乖說，訓義非所取，雖驗當時，不能通遠，又臣所未安也。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said: A calendar preserves effectiveness and fineness—it cannot tolerate different preferences; matching apocrypha and violating doctrine, interpretive meaning is not taken; though tested in its time, it cannot extend far—this again is what I am not settled about.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi said: A calendar preserves effectiveness and fineness—it cannot tolerate different preferences; matching apocrypha and violating doctrine, interpretive meaning is not taken; though tested in its time, it cannot extend far—this again is what I am not settled about.

sentences.zh: 元值始名，體明理正。

translations.literal: The origin value begins the name; the form is clear and principle correct.
translations.idiomatic: The origin value begins the name; the form is clear and principle correct.

sentences.zh: 未詳辛卯之說何依，古術詭謬，事在前牒，溺名喪實，殆非索隱之謂也。

translations.literal: I do not know on what the xinmao saying relies; ancient methods are strange and wrong—the matter is in the earlier memorial; drowning the name and losing the reality is hardly what seeking the hidden means.
translations.idiomatic: I do not know on what the xinmao saying relies; ancient methods are strange and wrong—the matter is in the earlier memorial; drowning the name and losing the reality is hardly what seeking the hidden means.

sentences.zh: 若以曆合一時，理無久用，元在所會，非有定歲者，今以效明之。

translations.literal: If because the calendar matches one time, principle has no long use—the origin lies where things meet, not in a fixed year—now I make it clear by effect.
translations.idiomatic: If because the calendar matches one time, principle has no long use—the origin lies where things meet, not in a fixed year—now I make it clear by effect.

sentences.zh: 夏、殷以前，載籍淪逸，《春秋》漢史，鹹書日蝕，正朔詳審，顯然可徵。

translations.literal: Before Xia and Yin, records were lost; the Spring and Autumn Annals and Han histories all record solar eclipses; correct new moon is examined in detail, clearly verifiable.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xia and Yin, records were lost; the Spring and Autumn Annals and Han histories all record solar eclipses; correct new moon is examined in detail, clearly verifiable.

sentences.zh: 以臣曆檢之，數皆協同，誠無虛設，循密而至，千載無殊，則雖遠知矣。

translations.literal: Testing by my calendar, the numbers all agree; truly no empty setting; following fineness to the end, a thousand years without difference—then though distant, it is known.
translations.idiomatic: Testing by my calendar, the numbers all agree; truly no empty setting; following fineness to the end, a thousand years without difference—then though distant, it is known.

sentences.zh: 備閱曩法，疏越實多，或朔差三日，氣移七晨，未聞可以下通於今者也。

translations.literal: Fully reading former methods, coarseness and distance are really many; some new moons miss three days, some qi shift seven lodges—I have not heard that one can extend downward to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Fully reading former methods, coarseness and distance are really many; some new moons miss three days, some qi shift seven lodges—I have not heard that one can extend downward to the present.

sentences.zh: 元在乙丑，前說以為非正，今值甲子，議者複疑其苟合，無名之歲，自昔無之，則推先者，將何從乎？

translations.literal: The origin in yichou—the earlier saying held it not correct; now the value is jiazi, and the debater again doubts a forced fit; a year without name never existed from old—then for pushing earlier, from what will one proceed?
translations.idiomatic: The origin in yichou—the earlier saying held it not correct; now the value is jiazi, and the debater again doubts a forced fit; a year without name never existed from old—then for pushing earlier, from what will one proceed?

sentences.zh: 曆紀之作，幾於息矣。

translations.literal: The making of calendar eras is nearly at an end.
translations.idiomatic: The making of calendar eras is nearly at an end.

sentences.zh: 夫為合必有不合，願聞顯據，以核理實。

translations.literal: For a fit there must be misfits—I wish to hear clear proof to examine principle and reality.
translations.idiomatic: For a fit there must be misfits—I wish to hear clear proof to examine principle and reality.

sentences.zh: 法興曰：「夫交會之元，則蝕既可求，遲疾之際，非凡夫所測。

translations.literal: Faxing said: "For the conjunction origin, eclipses can already be sought; for slow-fast junctures, this is not what ordinary men can measure.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing said: "From the conjunction origin eclipses can already be computed; slow-fast junctures are not what ordinary men can measure.

sentences.zh: 昔賈逵略見其差，劉洪粗著其術，至於疏密之數，莫究其極。

translations.literal: Formerly Jia Kui roughly saw their discrepancy; Liu Hong crudely set out their method; as for the numbers of density and fineness, none reached the ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui roughly saw their discrepancy; Liu Hong crudely set out their method; as for the fine and coarse numbers, none reached the ultimate.

sentences.zh: 且五緯所居，有時盈縮，即如歲星在軫，見超七辰，術家既追算以會今，則往之與來，斷可知矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the five planets' positions sometimes expand and contract; just as when Jupiter is in Chariot it appears seven lodges ahead, calendrists already trace calculation to match the present—then past and future can surely be known.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the five planets' positions sometimes expand and contract; when Jupiter is in Chariot it appears seven lodges ahead, and calendrists already trace calculation to match the present—past and future can surely be known.

sentences.zh: 《景初》所以紀首置差，《元嘉》兼又各設後元者，其並省功於實用，不虛推以為煩也。

translations.literal: Why Jingchu placed an initial discrepancy at the era-head and Yuanjia also set separate later origins was to save labor in practical use, not to push emptily and make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu placed an initial discrepancy at the era-head and Yuanjia set separate later origins to save labor in practical use, not to push emptily and make trouble.

sentences.zh: 沖之既違天于改易，又設法以遂情，愚謂此治曆之大過也。

translations.literal: Chongzhi both violates Heaven in reform and sets methods to suit his wishes; I deem this a great fault in governing the calendar."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi both violates Heaven in reform and sets methods to suit his wishes; I deem this a great fault in governing the calendar."

sentences.zh: 」沖之曰：遲疾之率，非出神怪，有形可檢，有數可推，劉、賈能述，則可累功以求密矣。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said: Slow-fast rates are not born from spirits and monsters; there is form that can be tested, numbers that can be pushed; if Liu and Jia could set them forth, one can accumulate work to seek fineness.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi said: Slow-fast rates are not born from spirits and monsters; there is form that can be tested, numbers that can be pushed; if Liu and Jia could set them forth, one can accumulate work to seek fineness.

sentences.zh: 議又雲「五緯所居，有時盈縮」。

translations.literal: The objection again says "the five planets' positions sometimes expand and contract."
translations.idiomatic: The objection again says "the five planets' positions sometimes expand and contract."

sentences.zh: 「歲星在軫，見超七辰」。

translations.literal: "When Jupiter is in Chariot it appears seven lodges ahead."
translations.idiomatic: "When Jupiter is in Chariot it appears seven lodges ahead."

sentences.zh: 謂應年移一辰也。

translations.literal: Meaning it ought to shift one lodge each year.
translations.idiomatic: Meaning it ought to shift one lodge each year.

sentences.zh: 案歲星之運，年恆過次，行天七匝，輒超一位。

translations.literal: Examining Jupiter's motion, each year it always passes its lodge; circling Heaven seven circuits, it suddenly advances one position.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Jupiter's motion, each year it always passes its lodge; circling Heaven seven circuits, it suddenly advances one position.

sentences.zh: 代以求之，曆凡十法，併合一時，此數咸同，史注所記，天驗又符。

translations.literal: Replacing generations to seek it, calendars in all ten methods combined at one time—this number is everywhere the same; history's annotated record and celestial tests again match.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing generations to seek it, calendars in all ten methods combined at one time—this number is everywhere the same; history's annotated record and celestial tests again match.

sentences.zh: 此則盈次之行，自其定準，非為衍度濫徙，頓過其沖也。

translations.literal: This is surplus-lodge motion from its fixed standard—not expanding degrees and recklessly shifting, suddenly passing its opposition.
translations.idiomatic: This is surplus-lodge motion from its fixed standard—not expanding degrees and recklessly shifting, suddenly passing its opposition.

sentences.zh: 若審由盈縮，豈得常疾無遲。

translations.literal: If it truly came from expansion and contraction, how could it always be fast without slow?
translations.idiomatic: If it truly came from expansion and contraction, how could it always be fast without slow?

sentences.zh: 夫甄耀測象者，必料分析度，考往驗來，准以實見，據以經史。

translations.literal: One who selects brilliance and measures images must calculate and analyze degrees, examine past and test future, standardize by real observation, rely on classics and history.
translations.idiomatic: One who selects brilliance and measures images must calculate and analyze degrees, examine past and test future, standardize by real observation, rely on classics and history.

sentences.zh: 曲辯碎說，類多浮詭，甘、石之書，互為矛盾。

translations.literal: Crooked argument and fragmentary talk are mostly floating and strange; the books of Gan and Shi mutually contradict.
translations.idiomatic: Crooked argument and fragmentary talk are mostly floating and strange; the books of Gan and Shi mutually contradict.

sentences.zh: 今以一句之經，誣一字之謬，堅執偏論，以罔正理，此愚情之所未厭也。

translations.literal: Now with one line from a classic to slander one character's error, stubbornly holding partial argument to obscure correct principle—this is what my humble mind has not yet tired of.
translations.idiomatic: Now with one line from a classic to slander one character's error, stubbornly holding partial argument to obscure correct principle—this is what my humble mind has not yet tired of.

sentences.zh: 算自近始，眾法可同，但《景初》之二差，承天之後元，實以奇偶不協，故數無盡同，為遺前設後，以從省易。

translations.literal: Calculation from the near start—many methods can agree; only Jingchu's two discrepancies, sub-epoch after matching Heaven, in fact because odd and even do not harmonize, therefore numbers cannot all match—setting former and later to follow simplification.
translations.idiomatic: Calculation from the near start—many methods can agree; only Jingchu's two discrepancies, sub-epoch after matching Heaven, in fact because odd and even do not harmonize, therefore numbers cannot all match—setting former and later to follow simplification.

sentences.zh: 夫建言倡論，豈尚矯異，蓋令實以文顯，言勢可極也。

translations.literal: Proposing words and initiating discussion—how could one esteem perverse difference; it is simply to make reality show through text, and speech reach its limit.
translations.idiomatic: Proposing words and initiating discussion—how could one esteem perverse difference; it is simply to make reality show through text, and speech reach its limit.

sentences.zh: 稽元曩歲，群數鹹始，斯誠術體，理不可容譏；

translations.literal: Examining the former origin year, all numbers begin—this is truly the method's form; principle cannot tolerate ridicule;
translations.idiomatic: Examining the former origin year, all numbers begin—this is truly the method's form; principle cannot tolerate ridicule;

sentences.zh: 而譏者以為過，謬之大者。

translations.literal: yet the ridiculer holds it excessive—the greater error.
translations.idiomatic: yet the ridiculer holds it excessive—the greater error.

sentences.zh: 然則《元嘉》置元，雖七率舛陳，而猶紀協甲子，氣朔俱終，此又過謬之小者也。

translations.literal: Then Yuanjia set the origin—though seven rates were wrongly arrayed, it still matched jiazi in the era, qi and new moon both ending—this again is the lesser excessive error.
translations.idiomatic: Then Yuanjia set the origin—though seven rates were wrongly arrayed, it still matched jiazi in the era, qi and new moon both ending—this again is the lesser excessive error.

sentences.zh: 必當虛立上元，假稱曆始，歲違名初，日避辰首，閏餘朔分，月緯七率，並不得有盡，乃為允衷之制乎？

translations.literal: Must one emptily set a superior origin, falsely call it calendar beginning, year violating name's start, day avoiding lodge head, intercalation remainder and new-moon fraction, moon's seven rates—all cannot be exhausted—then it is the balanced-center system?
translations.idiomatic: Must one emptily set a superior origin, falsely call it calendar beginning, year violating name's start, day avoiding lodge head, intercalation remainder and new-moon fraction, moon's seven rates—all cannot be exhausted—then it is the balanced-center system?

sentences.zh: 設法情實，謂意之所安；

translations.literal: Setting method's reality and intent means where the mind finds rest;
translations.idiomatic: Setting method's reality and intent means where the mind finds rest;

sentences.zh: 改易違天，未睹理之譏者也。

translations.literal: reforming and violating Heaven—I have not seen ridicule of principle.
translations.idiomatic: reforming and violating Heaven—I have not seen ridicule of principle.
